Sports.title: WBA World Title Bout Schofield vs Bahdi
Sports.content:
In the Golden Boy and Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) cross-promoted main event, a new champion will be crowned as Floyd Schofield will face Lucas Bahdi on Saturday night, October 10th, at the Wintrust Arena in Chicago, live on DAZN.

This matchup features two undefeated fighters who are both determined, hungry, and ready to take their careers to the next level. The winner of this highly anticipated lightweight fight will be awarded the vacant WBA world title.

Since signing with Golden Boy Promotions in August 2022, Floyd Schofield has made the transition from prospect to contender. In his most recent outing, a definitive statement was made as he stopped Tevin Farmer in the first round.

His October 10th opponent, Lucas Bahdi, didn’t have the luxury of being guided by a well-known promotional company. Bahdi was winning consistently, as he achieved most of his success under the radar.

Two years ago, Bahdi introduced himself to the mainstream when he knocked Ashton Sylve out cold in the sixth round. Now in a high-stakes matchup, Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-0, 15 KOs) is set to battle Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs).

Lucas Bahdi is a very patient fighter who is accurate, good at controlling range, has good timing, and has a powerful right hand. The fear for Bahdi is due to his economical punch output; he can get outworked and fall behind on the scorecards.

Floyd Schofield is athletic, has a solid jab, fast hands, throws a variety of combinations, and is a strong puncher. Schofield is a fast starter, but the question for Schofield is: can he sustain his energetic pace during the later rounds?

Now promoted by MVP, the Ontario, Canada native Lucas Bahdi knows a win on Saturday night will take his career to another level. Bahdi plans on representing and taking full advantage of the opportunity.

“I’m very proud to be Canadian. I wear that flag on my back when I enter the ring,” Bahdi said.”That was all part of the journey. Now here we are. We’re fighting for the world title and I’m ready.”

When the Austin, Texas product Floyd Schofield enters the ring on Saturday night, he will also be attempting to win his first world title. He appreciates the opportunity, and he appreciates the person that made it possible.

“This fight is for my pops. At the end of the day, he sacrificed his whole life for me just to be in this position. So I got a lot to prove Saturday,” Schofield said at the press conference.

On Saturday night, October 10th, the Schofield vs. Bahdi clash is guaranteed to be an action-packed event. Both men will enter the ring undefeated, but by the end of the night, somebody’s 0 has got to go.

Sports.title: Tex Cobb and Tyson Fury Keep Boxing Laughing
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury reminds me of Randall “Tex” Cobb for a reason that has little to do with championship belts. Both could make people laugh in a sport where the usual sales pitch involves threatening to knock somebody out.

With Fury preparing to face Anthony Joshua on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, there will be plenty of attention on what he has to say before the opening bell. His personality has long been part of the attraction.

Cobb had that same ability to hold an audience, although his humor often came at his own expense.

I remember watching him kick a heavy bag at Joe Frazier’s Broad Street gym in Philadelphia. He came from a kickboxing background, and seeing him at work offered a reminder that beneath the jokes was a tough, serious fighter.

His biggest boxing victory came in August 1980, when he stopped the feared Earnie Shavers in the eighth round. That win helped take Cobb toward a heavyweight title opportunity against Larry Holmes.

Holmes gave him a punishing beating over 15 rounds in November 1982. The bout helped prompt Howard Cosell to stop broadcasting professional boxing, rather than retire from broadcasting altogether. Cobb nevertheless found a way to turn his defeat into a punchline.

“Larry Holmes didn’t beat me. He just won the first fifteen rounds,” Cobb joked.

That line explains his appeal better than a list of opponents. Cobb could acknowledge a beating without asking anyone to feel sorry for him. His film and television work later gave that personality an audience beyond boxing.

Fury’s humor serves a different purpose. His teasing and boasting help sell fights and draw opponents into the conversation he wants to have. He has also achieved far more in the ring than Cobb, becoming heavyweight champion rather than remaining a contender.

Still, there are limits to what a personality can accomplish. Fury’s two defeats against Oleksandr Usyk cannot reasonably be blamed on his mouthing off. Usyk beat him through his work in the ring, where a clever remark offers no substitute for landing punches.

The connection between Cobb and Fury is their ability to give fans something to remember beyond a result. Cobb could lose badly and still leave people repeating his jokes. Fury can command attention long before he throws a punch.

Boxing needs skilled fighters, but its colorful characters give people another reason to follow them. Cobb understood that, and Fury has made it a large part of his career.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Accepts Offer for Jai Opetaia Fight
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder’s side has agreed to terms for a heavyweight meeting with Jai Opetaia on the Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua undercard, per Dan Rafael. That step nudges an odd co-feature closer to reality, even if the bout still needs an official green light.

Wilder’s manager, Shelly Finkel, told Rafael that their team gave the okay and is simply waiting on final sanctioning. Finkel noted that discussions regarding an encounter with Murat Gassiev occurred as well.

The proposal is on the table, though nothing is finalized. Wilder against Opetaia sounds nearly as bizarre as the debunked rumors pairing Manny Pacquiao with Shakur Stevenson. The difference is that paper exists here, even if the competitive logic feels thin.

Wilder is 40 and nearing the end of his run. Opetaia is 31, an elite cruiserweight jumping up in weight to take on an opponent whose marquee value outstrips his current form. Nearly a decade separates them, placing both men in drastically different stages of their journeys.

Wilder’s regression is well documented. The trademark right hand is dangerous against anyone stepping up in size, yet that single equalizer cannot carry the entire promotion. Defeats to Joseph Parker and Zhilei Zhang proved how quiet his offense becomes whenever foes take away his ideal launching lane.

Opetaia would certainly benefit from the spotlight of a massive pay-per-view platform. Even so, taking down an aging Wilder will tell observers very little about his viability against the division’s genuine contenders.

That reality exposes the flaw in the matchup. Wilder offers star power plus puncher’s luck. Opetaia brings youth and sharpness, but he has to jump weight classes just to make the attraction fit. Placing the bout on the undercard gives organizers another famous belt holder to market. It also highlights the growing sense that the event relies on nostalgic star power past its prime.

Finkel agreeing to the bout advances the paperwork, but it does nothing to turn this into a sensible contest. Putting him in with Opetaia only deepens the old-timers circus feel to the event. Opetaia is in his prime, fast, southpaw, and disciplined enough to pick apart a stationary target. Wilder getting outboxed or stopped by a cruiserweight moving up will not legitimize Opetaia as a real heavyweight threat; it will simply confirm that Wilder is completely washed up.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua Targets $34 Million Gate
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua’s December 11 fight in Cardiff is projected to generate a $34 million gate, Dana White told Sky Sports, putting the delayed heavyweight showdown on course for a British boxing record.

The figure shows how much commercial appeal remains in a fight that fans wanted years ago. Fury and Joshua are meeting later in their careers, but the opportunity to finally see them settle their rivalry has persuaded ticket buyers to spend heavily.

“I don’t want to mis-speak here but we have this thing scaled for around $34 million,” White told Sky Sports.

Regular tickets for the Principality Stadium event ranged from £88.50 to £13,128, excluding VIP, hotel and travel packages. White said fewer than 700 tickets remained on Friday evening after more than half a million people joined the Ticketmaster queue.

Those prices are a major part of the story. Filling a stadium demonstrates demand, but generating a record gate requires fans to pay enough across the seating plan. The projected revenue suggests the promoters have found buyers willing to treat Fury-Joshua as a major occasion despite the long wait.

For both fighters, that is the benefit of spending years becoming familiar names beyond boxing’s regular audience. Their previous defeats have changed how fans assess them in the ring, yet neither needs an unbeaten record to sell this particular matchup.

The unanswered question of who wins between them remains valuable. Fans who have followed the arguments for years now have a date and a venue, and the ticket response suggests many still want to witness the answer in person.

A record gate would underline how much business Fury and Joshua can still do together. It would also give promoters reason to pursue a second meeting if the first fight produces enough action or controversy to keep buyers interested.

For now, the $34 million remains a projection. The final receipts will determine the record, but the reported sales already show that the years of delays have not exhausted demand for Fury-Joshua.

Sports.title: Janibek Alimkhanuly Meets Jacob Bank for Vacant WBO Title
Sports.content:
Janibek Alimkhanuly now has a direct path to a belt at 168 pounds after the WBO confirmed terms are set for him to battle Jacob Bank for their vacant crown. Moving up provides Janibek another world title crack, while testing how well his middleweight firepower carries into the super middleweight ranks.

“DONE DEAL. Alimkhanuly vs. Bank for the vacant WBO Super Middleweight World Title!” the WBO announced on X.

The fight is reportedly headed to Copenhagen in December, although the WBO has yet to confirm the date, venue, or broadcaster.

Janibek has the edge in championship experience, but he still has to prove himself at 168. Bank gets the chance to test him against a bigger opponent and turn his first world title shot into the biggest win of his career.

If Bank can take Janibek’s power and keep pressing him, the former middleweight champion could have a difficult night. Janibek will need his jab and timing to control the exchanges rather than let Bank force him into a physical fight.

Bank gets the chance to make Janibek fight for every inch in this division. Taking out a hardened former middleweight champion gives Bank immediate legitimacy, proving he did more than pick up an abandoned strap. A victory also pushes his name into the mix for major work at 168 pounds.

Securing Copenhagen hands Bank true home-soil advantages. Fighting in front of his own people helps move tickets and guarantees strong local backing, but roaring fans will not solve the tactical problems Janibek presents once the bell rings.

Hamzah Sheeraz vacated the WBO title rather than face Janibek in an ordered defense. That opened the door for Bank, who now has a chance to win the belt against a former unified middleweight champion.

The date and venue still await confirmation. For Janibek, the fight tests whether he can reproduce his middleweight success at 168. Bank gets the chance to disrupt those plans and establish himself as champion.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Eyes Mexico Return With Herrera Waiting
Sports.content:
William Zepeda’s planned Mexico homecoming has a location and a timeframe, but Oscar De La Hoya has yet to name the opponent. With the WBC ordering Zepeda to face interim champion Jadier Herrera, that is the remaining detail in Golden Boy’s plans.

“We’re looking at the first quarter of next year. We are looking at fighting him in Mexico. I believe after his world title performance it deserves a homecoming for him in Mexico. So, we’re talking logistics with DAZN, with the whole team internal, and we’ll announce that soon,” De La Hoya told Fight Hub TV.

A Mexico return makes commercial sense for Zepeda. His pressure and punch output give Golden Boy an action fighter to promote, and bringing a championship defense home offers a chance to build an event around him.

However, arranging the venue and broadcast does not settle the opponent. The WBC has ordered the Herrera fight, with October 20 identified as the deadline for the camps to reach terms. No completed agreement was established in the reporting reviewed.

De La Hoya’s comments do not establish that Golden Boy intends to bypass Herrera. He was outlining a return plan rather than announcing a signed fight. Still, naming the challenger would give the homecoming a clearer sporting purpose.

Herrera’s interim title puts him in position to challenge Zepeda, and a meeting between them would resolve the WBC’s two-title situation at lightweight. It would also give the Mexico event a consequence beyond celebrating the champion’s previous performance.

For Herrera’s team, the venue would be part of the negotiation. Golden Boy wanting Mexico does not mean the challenger has accepted that location or the financial terms.

The first-quarter target leaves time to complete those arrangements. Until an opponent is confirmed, Zepeda’s homecoming remains a promotional plan awaiting its defining matchup. Herrera is the ordered challenger, and his inclusion would turn De La Hoya’s proposed celebration into a championship defense with something at stake.

Sports.title: Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson Fight for WBC Title
Sports.content:
Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson’s November 7 rematch will now produce a full WBC light heavyweight champion, with the sanctioning body confirming that the vacant belt will be at stake following David Benavidez’s decision to remain at cruiserweight.

The fight takes place at Manchester’s AO Arena, live on DAZN. Previously billed as an interim title contest, it now gives both fighters an opportunity to leave with the championship rather than wait for a shot at Benavidez.

That is a considerable improvement in the prize without an increase in the difficulty of the opponent. Neither man has to beat Benavidez to claim his former belt, although they still have an awkward fight against someone who knows their strengths.

Buatsi won their first meeting by split decision at Wembley Stadium in September 2024, putting Hutchinson down twice. Those knockdowns should be the starting point for assessing the rematch. Hutchinson had enough success to receive one judge’s vote, but his boxing did not keep him out of trouble when Buatsi connected.

For Hutchinson, winning more exchanges will only help if he can avoid giving those points back through trips to the canvas. He needs to control the distance while remaining active enough to win rounds. Spending too much time defending would allow Buatsi to dictate the pace and force him into another fight in which the heavier punches decide the outcome.

Buatsi has a different task. Having already beaten Hutchinson, he needs to reproduce the pressure and damaging work that brought him success without assuming the same openings will appear. Hutchinson has had two years to study where their first fight went wrong.

The title upgrade also changes the consequences of defeat. Losing an interim championship bout leaves a fighter chasing another route toward a championship. Losing this rematch means watching a familiar domestic rival take possession of a belt that became available when Benavidez moved on.

Their first fight established that Buatsi could hurt Hutchinson. The rematch will test whether Hutchinson can adjust enough to prevent that power from deciding who becomes world champion.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Seeks Long-Term Ryan Garcia Plan
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya still believes he can patch things up with Ryan Garcia. He wants a face-to-face sit-down to map out Garcia’s next five years. A real plan requires far more than settling personal grudges. It means picking the right opponents, setting a busy fight schedule, agreeing on a shared vision.

“It’s very salvageable. It’s a matter of talking to Ryan, sitting down with him, and mapping out his career for the next five years. I’m still hoping for that,” De La Hoya told Chris Mannix of DAZN.

Dana White presents a huge hurdle for that proposal. White wants to sign Ryan to Zuffa Boxing as soon as his current promotional deal expires. Garcia knocked out Conor Benn in September, prompting White to point out that only one Golden Boy bout remains on the table. That leaves De La Hoya chasing a massive commitment while a rival promoter circles.

Money talks here. Zuffa could throw a mountain of cash at Garcia, forcing Golden Boy to match those numbers. While nobody has confirmed an official Zuffa bid yet, White’s open pursuit gives Ryan every reason to test the market before signing away five prime years.

Ryan does not need a guru whispering in his ear to understand basic math. When guys like Conor Benn and Shakur Stevenson are pulling down massive purses under the Zuffa banner, Garcia is bound to take notice. Garcia brings mainstream eyes and instant revenue every time he steps in the ring.

Seeing Zuffa dump bags of cash on fighters who lack punch or fan appeal sends an unmistakable signal. If White is willing to overpay for them, Ryan’s market value to that outfit is through the roof. De La Hoya appeals to loyalty because it costs nothing. Golden Boy simply cannot compete with Dana White by offering sentiment, old memories, and long-term promises. Unless Oscar matches the sheer financial muscle Zuffa is flashing, Garcia has no business sticking around.

Ghana News.title: Ghana housing finance conference adopts communiqué to improve affordable housing access
Ghana News.content:
The National Conference on Housing Finance 2026 has adopted a communiqué committing government, financial institutions, housing developers, labour organisations and other stakeholders to coordinated action to improve access to affordable housing in Ghana.

The communiqué, adopted at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra on Thursday, October 8, outlines measures to address barriers to housing finance, promote affordable housing delivery and advance the goal of “Adequate Housing for All.”

The conference was convened by the National Housing Fund (NHF) in collaboration with public and private sector stakeholders, bringing together representatives of government, regulators, development partners, employers, academia and civil society.

Under the agreement, the NHF has been tasked with coordinating implementation of the commitments and monitoring progress.

The NHF pledged to promote innovation in the housing finance sector and expand access to financing for prospective homeowners and housing developers.

It committed to developing risk-sharing, guarantee, and other mechanisms to reduce financing barriers, as well as promoting affordable housing finance products for workers in both the formal and informal sectors.

The fund also plans to lead the establishment of a national homebuyers database and digital marketplace to connect housing demand with available homes and finance providers.

Other commitments include mobilising private investment, supporting social housing for vulnerable and underserved groups, and establishing mechanisms to monitor and report on progress.

Workers and labour organisations pledged to promote responsible savings and financial planning to support homeownership.

They also committed to participating in housing finance programmes and advocating for solutions that reflect the circumstances of workers in both formal and informal employment.

The groups said they would collaborate with government, the Ghana Real Estate Developers Association (GREDA), the NHF and financial institutions to develop sustainable pathways to affordable housing.

They further pledged to advocate for inclusive housing policies to ensure workers are not excluded from homeownership opportunities.

GREDA committed to promoting the use of appropriate local building materials and improving efficiency in housing delivery to help reduce construction costs and house prices.

The association also pledged to encourage green and climate-resilient building practices and collaborate with government, the NHF, financial institutions, workers and employers to develop affordable housing schemes.

The communiqué emphasises that improving access to adequate housing will require coordinated action on financing, land administration, urban planning, infrastructure, affordability, sustainability and institutional effectiveness.

It also calls for the commitments to be translated into measurable actions, with progress reviewed periodically and dialogue sustained among stakeholders.

“The Conference further commits to translating these resolutions into measurable actions, tracking progress periodically and sustaining dialogue among stakeholders to build an accessible, affordable, sustainable and inclusive housing finance system for Ghana,” the communiqué stated.

Ghana’s housing deficit has been estimated at more than 1.8 million units, while rapid urbanisation and rising construction costs continue to complicate efforts to provide affordable homes.

Access to housing finance remains a significant challenge, particularly for informal sector workers, many of whom may not have the regular income documentation or conventional employment arrangements required by traditional mortgage providers.

The conference sought to bring stakeholders across the housing sector together to identify coordinated responses to these challenges.

The NHF is expected to lead efforts to implement the agreed commitments and track progress towards the conference’s goal of adequate housing for all.

Ghana News.title: Special Initiatives Minister urges Wa Technical Institute to enrol more girls as EU-backed solar training lab opens
Ghana News.content:
Minister of State in charge of Special Initiatives at the Office of the President, Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo, has urged Wa Technical Institute to increase the enrolment of girls in renewable energy programmes, saying Ghana’s transition to green technology must create opportunities for both women and men.

He made the call at the launch of a solar photovoltaic (PV) training facility at the institute, established under the EU-Ghana Pact for Skills to strengthen practical training and prepare young people for jobs in the green economy.

The €17 million initiative, implemented by the European Union, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the Ghana TVET Service, seeks to bridge the gap between classroom instruction and practical skills development.

Dr Pelpuo said the opening of the facility should be judged not only by the equipment installed but also by the quality of training students receive, their competence after graduation and their ability to secure decent work.

“We are not simply opening a facility, commissioning equipment. We are strengthening the link between technical education, the green transition and the opportunity for decent work,” he said.

“The real test will not be what we see at the ceremony, but what follows. That is the quality of training provided, the competence of graduates, the services they provide and the opportunities they are able to access.”

Call for more women in renewable energy

Dr Pelpuo said women and girls must not be excluded from the opportunities emerging in renewable energy because technical trades have traditionally been dominated by men.

“New technologies, especially green technology taking over the world, must involve the female as much as the male,” he said.

He encouraged the institute and its partners to take deliberate steps to increase female participation in renewable energy training through targeted outreach, career guidance and an inclusive learning environment.

“Solar PV offers meaningful opportunities for women to develop technical competence, build careers and establish enterprises,” he said.

“Green skills must be inclusive skills. A stronger skills system identifies talents, develops it and gives every capable person a fair opportunity to be productive.”

From classroom theory to practical training

The new facility is expected to give students access to solar PV equipment for practical instruction in site assessment, installation, safety standards, performance testing, maintenance and troubleshooting.

The institute’s Principal, Seidu Saaka Adams, said the facility would address a longstanding gap in the teaching of solar technology.

“For a long time, we were teaching solar with no solar equipment. This lab changes everything,” he said.

“Imagination alone cannot make a technician. You must see, you must touch, and you must do.”

The facility also includes training for instructors, improved connectivity to support blended learning and activities aimed at integrating environmental sustainability into technical and vocational education and training (TVET).

EU and ILO stress investment in people

EU Team Leader for the Pact for Skills, Gisela Spreitzhofer, said the project formed part of a broader €17 million investment intended to help create green and digital jobs for young people in Ghana.

ILO Country Director for Nigeria, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone, Dr Vanessa Phala-Moyo, said the success of the initiative would depend on more than the provision of equipment.

“Equipment is only an enabler. What we have here is a complete, comprehensive value chain,” she said, citing the combination of modern solar PV equipment, curriculum support, instructor development, practical installation, digital connectivity and greener TVET delivery.

“Technology must go hand in hand with investment in people,” she added.

Dr Pelpuo called for the institute and its partners to monitor how effectively the facility is used and whether the training meets the needs of employers.

He said underused equipment should prompt action to address barriers, while difficulties faced by graduates in finding work should lead to a review of the relationship between training and labour-market demand.

He added that emerging skills requirements should inform curriculum development and instructor training.

The facility is expected to strengthen practical solar training at Wa Technical Institute as demand grows for renewable energy skills among households, businesses and public institutions adopting solar technology.

Ghana News.title: In the matter of my first year at the Bar
Ghana News.content:
A reflection on my first year at the Bar

Looking Back

A year ago, I heard my name read out as a member of the Bar in Ghana. Twelve months in the Court of Appeal, the High Court and the Circuit Court have since taught me more than the long years of preparation that came before. What follows is what I have learnt, written for myself and for the lawyers who will be called this Friday.

What the Rules Do Not Tell You

The rules of procedure give a court its skeleton, but the room has a living body. Judges have habits and registries have rhythms. A motion flawless on paper can still lose a day because service never reached the other side. I confirm the cause list the day before and carry spare copies. The lawyers I admire most are rarely the loudest in court. They go about their work diligently and calmly.

Moving between the High Court and the Circuit Court almost every other day has shown me they reward different instincts. The High Court wants authority and tidy bundles. The Circuit Court, particularly in family matters, sits closer to the people whose lives are in the balance, and a petitioner in a matrimonial cause wants to know when it will end.

The Long Wait for Justice

Nobody warns you how much of litigation is waiting. The other party has not been served, and a date three months away is announced as though it were good news. Clients do not understand this, and I no longer blame them. We share the blame for our adjournment culture whenever we ask for time we do not truly need. I mean to be ready on the day and to tell clients the truth about delay early.

The First Monday

Everything I believe about this work traces back to one morning. The call to the Bar is a day of gowns, photographs and relatives who have waited years to hear your name. What I remember is the telephone call that evening, when my senior told me to be at a Circuit Court on Monday. A judgment was due in one of his matters, and he wanted me there- alone.

Nobody hands a lawyer of three days anything to argue on judgment day, yet I walked in as though the whole building had come to watch me. I took a seat at the bar and opened a new notebook. Then the judge began to read. I had read hundreds of judgments on paper and never once listened to one. I wrote furiously, because my senior would plan his next move from my notes. That Monday taught me what the profession expects first of a junior: to hear correctly and report faithfully.

Standing Up to Speak

My first time on my feet alone to move a motion was an application for substituted service. I rehearsed for two days and still stumbled over the opening sentence. The judge waited, not unkindly, and asked a question that cut through it all: what exactly did I want the court to do, and why could the other side not be served in the ordinary way? I told the court, and the rest came easily. If you cannot state your application in two sentences, you do not yet understand it.

Before the Three Pillars of Justice

The Court of Appeal is another world. The room is quieter and the questions come from three directions at once. On appeal you argue about whether the law was rightly applied, before a panel that has usually read the record more closely than you would like. On one occasion I went alone to hear judgment before the three pillars of Justice, thought of that first Monday, and was conscious of the distance.

Building Before Earning

Money is not a dirty word at the Bar. Rent has to be paid, and a junior who pretends otherwise is either supported by someone else or is not honest. But a lawyer chasing the quickest fee will pay for it later. The brief that pays fast often teaches nothing, and the junior who takes every matter, soon learns how expensive cheap money can be.

The early years are an apprenticeship. Every hour in court behind a senior and every draft returned covered in corrections is training no tuition could buy. The Bar has its shortcuts; undercutting colleagues, accepting matters beyond your competence, promising results no honest lawyer can promise. Each spends reputation, which a young practitioner cannot buy back. Take the money you are fairly owed, and do not let it become the reason you stopped learning.

The Other Desk

Alongside the practice, I have kept up my passion for writing articles, mostly on football, and the two have competed for the same hours. A hearing in the morning and a piece due by evening looks manageable in a diary and feels different at half past ten at night. The law is a jealous profession, and no deadline is a good reason to walk into court half-prepared, so the days belong to the practice and the writing takes what the nights will give. Yet I would not give up either. Writing has made me clearer in submissions, and court has made me wary of publishing any claim I could not defend.

What I Take With Me

The profession is smaller than it looks. The opponent who frustrates you today will be the colleague you need next month, and the clerk or bailiff who sees your manners will remember them. Be courteous without being soft, and never tell a court anything you would be embarrassed to defend. Credibility is the only capital a young lawyer truly owns.

I owe much to my seniors, my brother Andrew Khartey and Elikem Adisenu-Doe, who let me watch before they let me speak, and who corrected me in private and praised me in front of others. Having been taught that way, I intend to teach that way. I am not yet the lawyer I mean to become, but I know what the work demands: preparation no one sees, honesty that costs something, and patience. The Monday after my call was a quiet beginning, and I am grateful it began with listening.

A Word to the Newly Called

Congratulations to the 1400 to be called to the Bar on Friday, especially my cousin David Andreas Hesse Jnr and my friends Samuel Kyeremeh, Daisy Hanson-Nortey and Anne Adjasah. The years of study and the sacrifices of the family members who will fill the auditorium all arrive at a single morning, and you have earned every minute of it. Enjoy it, and thank the people who carried you here. Then on Monday, go and find a courtroom, sit behind someone who knows more than you do, and listen. Be patient with the money and serious about the law, and the profession will repay you in ways a quick fee never could. Welcome to the Bar.

Ghana News.title: ActionAid Ghana calls for an end to child marriage, greater investment in girls’ rights
Ghana News.content:
ActionAid Ghana has called for stronger measures to end child marriage and school-related abuse, urging government and community leaders to invest more in girls’ rights, education and leadership.

The call was made during the 2026 International Day of the Girl-Child celebration in Techiman, Bono East Region, held under the theme “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights.”

Addressing traditional leaders, educators, students and other stakeholders, ActionAid Ghana’s Regional Programme Manager, Kwame Afram Denkyira, said girls should be recognised as rights-holders and agents of change rather than victims in need of rescue.

“We say ayikoo to our girls,” he said. “Girls are not victims to be saved but rights holders and agents of liberation who deserve justice, resources, and power.”

Mr Denkyira identified school-related gender-based violence, early and forced marriage, digital exclusion and the effects of climate change and austerity measures among the challenges confronting girls.

He said recent cases of sexual abuse in schools reflected deeper structural inequalities and failures that required accountability and action.

According to him, silence, impunity and patriarchal power can protect perpetrators at the expense of survivors, making it necessary to strengthen systems that safeguard girls and ensure justice.

Techiman Municipal Girl-Child Coordinator Ellen White Opoku said ending child marriage required a collective effort involving parents, traditional authorities, religious leaders and law enforcement agencies.

She called for decisive action against perpetrators, warning that abuse and exploitation could deprive girls of their childhood and limit their future opportunities.

ActionAid Ghana urged the government, Parliament, local authorities and traditional leaders to take practical steps to protect girls and expand their opportunities.

The organisation called for stronger accountability for child marriage and abuse, survivor-centred support and safer, gender-responsive schools.

It also urged increased investment in quality education, mentorship, healthcare and digital access, particularly for girls in rural communities.

Other recommendations included the full implementation of existing child protection laws, including the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), and the adoption of gender-responsive budgets that prioritise girls’ rights and leadership.

A message from ActionAid Ghana’s Country Director reinforced the organisation’s position that investment in girls should be treated as a matter of justice rather than charity.

“Girls in Ghana are not victims to be rescued; they are rights-holders and leaders who are shaping the future of our country,” the message stated.

“Girls are not the future; they are the leaders of today. When we deliver justice and tear down barriers, their power transforms our country.”

ActionAid Ghana reaffirmed its commitment to working with traditional authorities, education stakeholders and communities in the Bono East Region to advance equality, dignity and justice for girls.

Ghana News.title: Newsfile to tackle World Cup visa scandal, beach demolitions, education strikes, BRICS bid
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile, will on Saturday, October 10, examine four major national issues that have dominated public discussion over the past week.

Hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, the programme will air from 8:00am to 12:00 noon on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms.

The discussions will focus on allegations surrounding Ghana’s 2026 FIFA World Cup visa arrangements, demolitions along the La Beach area, strikes disrupting education, and the country’s bid to join the BRICS economic bloc.

World Cup visa controversy: EOCO probe or cover-up?

The programme will examine allegations by the Minority in Parliament over Ghana’s visa arrangements connected to activities surrounding the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

At a press conference on Wednesday, October 7, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, alleged that some individuals paid between US$7,000 and US$14,000 for visa processing.

The Minority also questioned the verification of personnel whose names were submitted by the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) and the National Sports Authority (NSA) to the US and Canadian embassies.

It alleged that only two of 50 names submitted by the GTA as media personnel were verified as professional media practitioners, while 15 of 102 names submitted by the NSA were verified as actual employees.

President John Dramani Mahama has asked former NSA Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah to step aside, with Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong appointed acting Director-General.

The Ministry of Sports and Recreation has provided a chronology of its engagements, citing correspondence dated January 28, 2026, which it says shows that some arrangements connected to the World Cup fan experience predated its involvement.

The programme will examine the allegations, the responses from the institutions involved and calls for further investigation.

Beach demolitions: Who is accountable?

The second topic will focus on the demolition of structures along the La Beach area in Accra, including La Pleasure Beach and the Polo Beach Club near the Labadi Beach Hotel.

The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has defended the operation, saying it sought the intervention of the National Security Council Secretariat over what it described as persistent unlawful occupation, encroachment and unauthorised activities on the beachfront adjoining the Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel.

SSNIT said the two hotels formed part of its investment portfolio and were significant national hospitality and tourism assets that it had a responsibility to protect.

“These assets belong to the workers and pensioners of Ghana,” the Trust stated.

However, Deputy Chief of Staff Stan Dogbe said the operation was not part of the government’s flood mitigation exercise, explaining that it was conducted under National Security supervision at the request of the Labadi Beach Hotel.

The Ghana Journalists Association has also condemned alleged attacks on journalists covering the demolitions and given the Ghana Armed Forces two weeks to account for the actions of its personnel.

Newsfile will examine the circumstances surrounding the operation, questions of accountability and the concerns raised by affected parties.

Education crisis: Two strikes, who pays the price?

The programme will also discuss the impact of strikes by pre-tertiary teachers and university administrators on Ghana’s education system.

The three pre-tertiary teacher unions — the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) — have been on strike since September 25 over delayed promotions, deprived-area allowances and negotiations on a new collective bargaining agreement.

A meeting between the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission and union leadership on Tuesday, October 6, ended without an agreement.

Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has pledged that the salary grades of at least 51,000 promoted teachers will be validated and their arrears paid by October 16 through a supplementary intervention.

“If by October 30, your promotion arrears are not paid, then I will have no honour,” he stated.

Meanwhile, the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) has been on strike for more than two months, disrupting administrative services at public universities.

University of Ghana Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Gordon Awandare has warned that the academic calendar could collapse if the strike extends into the following week.

“The reality is that currently many of the systems are not working because they are managed by members of GAUA who are on strike,” he said.

The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has also postponed its reopening indefinitely because of the strike.

The discussion will consider the unresolved grievances, the impact on students and the prospects for ending the industrial actions.

Ghana’s BRICS bid: What does it mean for national interest?

The fourth topic will examine Ghana’s formal application to join the BRICS economic bloc, announced by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa.

The Minority in Parliament has called for an urgent briefing on the decision, seeking clarity on its geopolitical implications and potential consequences for Ghana’s national interests.

The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has questioned why Ghana is seeking full membership rather than following Nigeria’s approach as a BRICS partner country.

“Why is it that we are not taking the path of Nigeria, which is a partner country of BRICS and not a full member?” he asked.

Mr Ablakwa has defended the application, arguing that membership could broaden Ghana’s development and diplomatic options.

“BRICS offers us that opportunity to have options in our development agenda. We value our traditional relationships, but we must have new friends,” he said.

India’s External Affairs Minister, Dr S. Jaishankar, has welcomed Ghana’s interest, while noting that an expansion decision requires consensus among existing BRICS members.

The panel will examine the potential opportunities and implications of the bid, including its relationship with Ghana’s existing international partnerships.

Newsfile, hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, airs on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms from 8:00am to 12:00 noon on Saturday, October 10, 2026.

Ghana News.title: UK-Ghana Trade & Investment Summit: Trade Resource Centre to help businesses maximise UK-Ghana trade opportunities
Ghana News.content:
Executive Director of the UKGCC, Adjoba Kyiamah, in a symbolic handshake with Eugene T. Sangmortey, UK-Ghana JET Team Lead, at the launch of the Trade Resource Centre

In a significant boost to UK-Ghana trade and investment relations, the UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC), in partnership with the UK-Ghana Jobs and Economic Transformation (JET) Programme, has launched the UK-Ghana Trade Resource Centre, a practical market-access platform designed to help businesses identify opportunities, navigate export requirements and build commercial partnerships between Ghana and the United Kingdom.

The UK and Ghana enjoy strong trade relations, with total bilateral trade reaching approximately £1.6 billion in the year to Q1 2026. Yet, despite this progress, significant untapped opportunities remain for businesses in both countries. The Trade Resource Centre has been established to help bridge information gaps, connect businesses with the right partners, and support firms to take greater advantage of opportunities under the UK-Ghana Trade Partnership Agreement.

The launch formed one of the major outcomes of the UK-Ghana Trade & Investment Summit 2026, a three-day event which brought together government leaders, investors, business executives and trade stakeholders from both countries under the theme, “A Decade of Trust, A Future Always On: Scaling the UK-Ghana Growth Partnership.”

Speaking at the launch, the Executive Director of the UKGCC, Adjoba Kyiamah, described the Centre as a significant step toward addressing the information and market-access challenges faced by businesses seeking to trade between Ghana and the United Kingdom.

"The Trade Resource Centre represents our commitment to moving beyond conversations about trade and providing businesses with practical support to succeed. Whether a Ghanaian exporter is looking to access the UK market or a UK company is seeking opportunities in Ghana, the Centre will provide the guidance, connections, and market intelligence needed to make those journeys easier and more successful," Ms. Kyiamah remarked.

The Trade Resource Centre has been established as a core UKGCC function aimed at helping Ghana and UK businesses navigate the bilateral trade landscape, connect with the right partners and maximise opportunities under the UK-Ghana Trade Partnership Agreement (TPA). It will operate as a practical support platform providing guidance, market intelligence, business linkages and trade facilitation services

Benefit to Exporters and Importers

The Centre is expected to be particularly beneficial to exporters and importers seeking to take advantage of opportunities created by the UK-Ghana TPA.

For export-ready Ghanaian businesses, the Centre will provide market-specific guidance, export readiness support, referrals to technical expertise, and connections to British buyers and commercial networks. It will also work with partners to identify export-ready firms and facilitate business matchmaking opportunities.

On the other hand, importers and UK businesses interested in sourcing from Ghana will gain access to market intelligence, industry networks, partner referrals and commercial linkage support designed to improve trade flows between both countries.

The Centre will also collaborate with key institutions including the UK’s Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) in Accra, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), sector associations, and finance providers to ensure businesses receive coordinated support.

Economic Impact

Speaking on behalf of the UK- Ghana Jobs and Economic Transformation (JET) Programme, Eugene Sangmortey, Team Lead, said the initiative aligned with broader efforts to strengthen trade competitiveness and support private-sector growth.

"The UK remains an important trade partner for Ghana; leveraging the TPA to deepen access to the UK market for Ghanaian manufacturers and exporters is crucial to business growth, trade diversification, job creation and economic transformation. The Trade Resource Centre is that practical mechanism that will drive achievement of this ambition and support exporters to overcome information barriers, improve export market readiness, and connect with viable opportunities that will drive growth, unlock investment and create quality jobs."

Mr. Sangmortey also highlighted UK-Ghana JET’s strategic role in supporting Ghana’s industrial transformation, noting that through their support, in the form of technical assistance, the government has approved industrial policy frameworks covering automotive components manufacturing, textiles and garments and pharmaceuticals.

These frameworks will be instrumental in strengthening Ghana’s manufacturing ecosystem, attract investment and create thousands of jobs when fully implemented.

Strengthening the Growth Partnership

The launch of the Trade Resource Centre reinforces the growing focus on translating the UK-Ghana Growth Partnership into tangible commercial outcomes and follows discussions throughout the Summit on investment promotion, trade facilitation, market access, and business expansion.

Industry stakeholders at the Summit described the Centre as one of the most practical outcomes of the event, with the potential to improve access to information, reduce transaction barriers and strengthen the participation of businesses in UK-Ghana trade.

The three-day UK-Ghana Trade and Investment Summit 2026 is being supported by leading institutions and businesses, including GCB Bank PLC, PwC Ghana LTD., UK Government's flagship Ghana Jobs and Economic Transformation (JET) programme, Fidelity Bank Ghana LTD., Ecobank Ghana PLC, Vivo Energy Ghana LTD., Quao Realty, DMA Invest, Aqua Africa, Guinness Ghana Breweries PLC, UniChem Ghana LTD., Kasapreko PLC, and media partner, The Business Year.

Ghana News.title: Embassy of Denmark celebrates World Maritime Day
Ghana News.content:
The Embassy of Denmark in Accra has hosted an event to celebrate World Maritime Day and mark the 10-year hallmark for the Danish Maritime Security Programme for the Gulf of Guinea.

The event, which brought together partners from across the maritime security, commercial, and regulatory sectors, was accompanied by a superb exhibition of maritime art.

This year’s World Maritime Day is themed, “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence”. It mirrors Denmark’s decade-long effort to translate international maritime policies into tangible action in the Gulf of Guinea. The Denmark Ambassador to Ghana, Jakob Linulf, highlighted Denmark’s strategic collaboration with Ghana in maritime.

“As a seafaring nation, Denmark understands the importance of safe seas, freedom of navigation, and a rules-based maritime order. For a decade now, Denmark has worked closely with Ghana to ensure today’s safe and open sea lanes in Gulf of Guinea, which are vital for international trade, economic development, and the livelihoods of millions of people”, Ambassador Linulf stated,

Denmark in 2026 commenced the implementation of the Danish Maritime Security Programme for the Gulf of Guinea, funded through the Danish Peace and Stabilization Fund. Now in its third phase (2022-2026), the programme addresses the full maritime criminal justice chain through a comprehensive approach combining diplomacy, development assistance, and military support, in close partnership with national, regional, and international actors, including Ghana.

Under the programme, Denmark’s support is centred on three pillars. The first being, Normative work, supporting the development of strategic, legal, and operational frameworks for maritime security and governance, in line with regional and international frameworks. Examples are the Yaoundé Code of Conduct, UNCLOS, and the SUA Convention.

The second isCapacity building, for both military personnel, including Ghana Navy’s Special Boat Squadron, and civilian actors in law enforcement, prosecution, and inter-agency coordination, delivered through partners such as UNODC, INTERPOL, KAIPTC, and Royal Danish Defence College. The final focuses on Equipment and infrastructure support, strengthening the operational capability of regional and national maritime security institutions.

As a seafaring nation, Denmark remains firmly committed to international legal and policy frameworks that promote freedom of navigation, maritime safety, and the protection of seafarers, a commitment underscored by the fact that approximately 90% of global trade by volume is transported by sea.

A maritime-themed art exhibition presented three commissioned works by Ghanaian and international artists, Emmanuel Aggrey Tieku, Fang Wang Linulf, and Patrick Tagoe-Turkson, exploring maritime pollution, ocean-borne waste, and the lived coastal realities of the Gulf of Guinea, raising awareness of ocean ecology, coastal memory and the human dimensions of maritime governance.

Embassy of Denmark celebrates World Maritime Day

The Embassy of Denmark in Accra has hosted an event to celebrate World Maritime Day and mark the 10-year hallmark for the Danish Maritime Security Programme for the Gulf of Guinea.

The event, which brought together partners from across the maritime security, commercial, and regulatory sectors, was accompanied by a superb exhibition of maritime art.

This year’s World Maritime Day is themed, “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence”. It mirrors Denmark’s decade-long effort to translate international maritime policies into tangible action in the Gulf of Guinea. The Denmark Ambassador to Ghana, Jakob Linulf highlighted Denmark’s strategic collaboration with Ghana in maritime.

“As a seafaring nation, Denmark understands the importance of safe seas, freedom of navigation, and a rules-based maritime order. For a decade now, Denmark has worked closely with Ghana to ensure today’s safe and open sea lanes in Gulf of Guinea, which are vital for international trade, economic development, and the livelihoods of millions of people”, Ambassador Linulf stated,

Denmark in 2026 commenced the implementation of the Danish Maritime Security Programme for the Gulf of Guinea, funded through the Danish Peace and Stabilization Fund. Now in its third phase (2022-2026), the programme addresses the full maritime criminal justice chain through a comprehensive approach combining diplomacy, development assistance, and military support, in close partnership with national, regional, and international actors, including Ghana.

Under the programme, Denmark’s support is centred on three pillars. The first being, Normative work, supporting the development of strategic, legal, and operational frameworks for maritime security and governance, in line with regional and international frameworks. Examples are the Yaoundé Code of Conduct, UNCLOS, and the SUA Convention.

The second isCapacity building, for both military personnel, including Ghana Navy’s Special Boat Squadron, and civilian actors in law enforcement, prosecution, and inter-agency coordination, delivered through partners such as UNODC, INTERPOL, KAIPTC, and Royal Danish Defence College. The final focuses on Equipment and infrastructure support, strengthening the operational capability of regional and national maritime security institutions.

As a seafaring nation, Denmark remains firmly committed to international legal and policy frameworks that promote freedom of navigation, maritime safety, and the protection of seafarers, a commitment underscored by the fact that approximately 90% of global trade by volume is transported by sea.

A maritime-themed art exhibition presented three commissioned works by Ghanaian and international artists, Emmanuel Aggrey Tieku, Fang Wang Linulf, and Patrick Tagoe-Turkson, exploring maritime pollution, ocean-borne waste, and the lived coastal realities of the Gulf of Guinea, raising awareness of ocean ecology, coastal memory and the human dimensions of maritime governance.

Ghana News.title: Linking LEAP to productive inclusion could cut extreme poverty by 2030 – UNICEF
Ghana News.content:
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) says linking Ghana’s Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme with the Productive Inclusion Initiative (PII) could reduce extreme poverty by 2.5 percentage points by 2030.

The organisation is urging the government to ensure that social protection laws translate into tangible support for vulnerable households.

The call was made at the launch of the Social Protection Act, 2025, and the Social Protection and Affirmative Action Regulations in Accra on October 7, 2026.

UNICEF welcomed the Act’s emphasis on coordination and complementarity, saying stronger links between social protection programmes could help address the multiple challenges facing vulnerable families.

“We have evidence that when paired, the LEAP and PII programs have the potential to reduce extreme poverty by two and a half percentage points by 2030,” the organisation said.

UNICEF illustrated the need for coordinated support with the example of a young mother whose household struggles with limited income and the cost of essential services.

“She may be struggling with her income but also with the cost of nutritious food, access to health care, child care, skills, education, employment,” it said.

The example highlights how vulnerable households can face several interconnected challenges that cash assistance alone may not fully address.

The Social Protection Act provides for social assistance and social insurance, establishes institutional arrangements and creates a social protection fund.

Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged stakeholders to address gaps that limit access to social protection programmes to ensure assistance reaches its intended beneficiaries.

The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection is responsible for implementing the frameworks.

Sector Minister Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey assured that the ministry would prioritise effective implementation and monitoring to help alleviate poverty and improve livelihoods.

She said the ministry would make the laws accessible through clear language and local-language translations, with outreach across regions and districts to help citizens understand their rights and responsibilities.

“We will support institutions to comply by providing clear guidance, practical tools, reporting templates and training for the officers who apply these rules each day,” she said.

Dr Lartey added that the ministry would strengthen data systems to support fair beneficiary targeting, improve governance of the social protection fund and establish accessible complaint channels that citizens could trust.

The frameworks are expected to improve the delivery of social protection programmes and help ensure support reaches vulnerable people who need it most.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
