World.title: CNN, MS Now, Politico urge judge to extend White House access
World.content:
Washington – CNN, MS NOW and Politico urged a federal judge on Thursday to extend White House access to the three media outlets which President Donald Trump is seeking to ban.

District Judge Timothy Kelly prolonged until Tuesday the temporary White House access he granted to the news organizations last month and said he expected to issue a ruling by then.

Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House on September 18 for distributing what he called “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”

The three outlets filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico appeared in a downtown Washington court on Thursday to ask that the judge transform his TRO into a preliminary injunction prohibiting Trump from barring them from the White House while the case proceeds.

Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer for the media outlets, said Trump issued the ban “because of what he perceives as negative, false, bad, not positive enough reporting.”

The Republican president, Boutrous said, apparently “got up on the wrong side of the bed and declared a ban on these news organizations.”

“He doesn’t like scrutiny of his policies. He doesn’t like the reporting. He wants more good press,” he said. “If your press pass is at risk because President Trump decides something you said is false, that’s a very, very dangerous, chilling doctrine.”

Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik, urging the judge to uphold the ban, accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of violating “journalistic standards” and endangering national security by revealing classified information.

A skeptical Kelly asked Velchik whether it was a “a violation of minimum journalistic standards to portray the administration in a negative light?”

In his ruling last month temporarily restoring the White House credentials of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, the judge, who was appointed by Trump during his first term, said the ban “likely violated their constitutional due process rights.”

Trump has long attacked media that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.”

Following the judge’s order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico were granted access to the White House grounds and the briefing room but have been kept out of the Oval Office and Air Force One.

In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters — ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC — halted pool coverage of the White House — where a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day — in solidarity with CNN.

World.title: OpenAI says Iran, Russia influence ops busted
World.content:
Washington – OpenAI on Thursday said it shut down two influence operations — from Russia and Iran — that used ChatGPT to push fake journalist personas and run a “think-tank” to covertly peddle anti-Ukraine propaganda.

OpenAI’s report is the latest illustration of how state actors can easily exploit widely available AI tools to peddle sophisticated propaganda against adversaries on a mass scale.

The American AI giant said it banned a cluster of ChatGPT accounts that originated in Russia and Iran and were used to support “false front” entities for geopolitical and conflict-related messaging.

The Iranian operation involved seven “journalist” profiles, each purporting to be from Western countries including the United States, that were used to plant long-form articles in media outlets around the world.

“We identified almost 100 articles published or syndicated under the operation’s bylines across roughly a dozen online outlets around the world,” OpenAI said.

“These were small to medium outlets, generally focused on international affairs, geopolitics, and events in the Middle East.”

The earliest article identified by OpenAI was published in July 2025, and the latest in October 2026, with the frequency of reports increasing after the US-Iran war broke out earlier this year.

The operation also generated social media comments on topics related to the US-Iran war, it added.

One of the personas named Ervin B. Hoskins, whose bio claimed to be “an American freelance writer,” had social media accounts across tech platforms including Elon Musk’s X and Meta-owned Instagram.

X’s transparency information showed the account was connected via a “West Asia android app” and Instagram’s transparency information showed the account was based in Iran, according to screenshots provided by OpenAI.

Both accounts appeared to be suspended.

The Russian operation co-opted “unwitting people” in Latin America to run a “think-tank” — called the Social Research Center (SRC) — used for covert activities aimed at undermining Ukraine’s reputation in the region and to influence local politics, the company said.

“The available evidence indicates that the SRC’s employees in Latin America were not aware that they were working for a Russian group,” OpenAI said.

“The SRC appears to have produced a majority of original content via its co-opted staff. This stands out as the most complex attempt to run a front identity that we’ve disrupted over the past two and a half years.”

World.title: Before CJP protest, Delhi bandh: Mobile net, metro, roads blocked in heart of city
World.content:

NEW DELHI: Checks at Delhiâs borders and barricaded roads inside, mobile internet snapped and metro stations shut â Delhi Police has put in place stringent measures to stop protesters from gathering at Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning. Central Delhi looked like an impregnable fortress by Friday night.The fortified city is expected to see around 35,000 security personnel, including those from Delhi Police and paramilitary forces, to stop what the authorities estimate will be a crowd of 20,000 from reaching Jantar Mantar. The protest is scheduled to start at 10am. Police sources said extra forces were requested because the gathering during the Cockroach Janta Party protest in June-July had been âunderestimatedâ.Mobile internet services in a 4km radius from the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing were snapped at 10pm on Friday. The curbs will continue till 10pm on Saturday. Entry and exit at 57 metro stations (later reduced to 45) were stopped till further notice, after Delhi Policeâs Transport Range wrote to Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, citing the possibility of âunruly crowd movement towards sensitive locationsâ.Apart from this, more than 30 blockade points â including some at the borders â have been identified.âThose attempting to create anarchy or move towards the protest site will be detained immediately. The plan is to stop them at the cityâs borders,â an officer said.Joint CP Nupur Prasad said CJP submitted its request to hold a protest on Saturday at âvery short noticeâ and hence permission could not be granted. The application was received on Oct 7. âAs per the prescribed guidelines, such applications must be submitted at least 10 days before the protest,â she said.Referring to the June-July protests, JCP Nupur Prasad said, âOn an earlier occasion, when CJP was granted permission to hold a protest, they failed to follow lawful directions and adhere to the undertakings they had submitted. Consequently, in view of their failure to comply with legal directions and undertakings, and considering the current requirements for maintaining public safety, law and order and traffic regulations, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar has been denied. âCJP co-convener Saurav Das, however, said the police had known about the protest since Oct 2 when they had announced it. The 10-day timeline is to ensure that adequate security forces are deployed and traffic arrangements are made, he said, pointing out that even before Oct 2, forces had been deployed as other outfits were protesting on the same issue.âThis shows that all of this is an excuse. And we vehemently disagree with the very concept of seeking âpermissionâ from govt to protest against it. Itâs absurd and doesnât make any sense. Itâs a colonial mindset,â he said.Personnel at some entry points have been asking motorists about their destinations to keep a check on any movement towards central Delhi.Joint Commissioner of Police (Northern Range) Madhur Verma posted on X Friday: âPrepare for the storm. Practise restraint. Protect the peace. Because the true strength of the police is not merely in controlling a crowd, but in doing so with discipline, dignity and minimum force.âDelhi Police also posted an open letter to citizens on X Friday, invoking duty and humanity, asking people to remember that police personnel have families too.An AI-generated image of a postcard appeared with the message: âAapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki suraksha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska apna parivar hai, apne log hain. Faraq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi (Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is a person who has a family and own people. The only difference is the uniform, not humanity).âIn a detailed note, Delhi Police justified the curbs put in place: âThe right to peaceful protest is an important democratic right. At the same time, New Delhi houses important establishments and offices of constitutional authorities and the safety and convenience of residents, workers, commuters and businesses must also be protected.Delhi Police is responsible for safeguarding all these interests while maintaining public order,â it said.âThe circumstances surrounding the protests held at Jantar Mantar in July must be taken into consideration. Permission had reportedly been granted for a one-day protest, but the gathering continued for approximately a month. During this period, more than 200 police personnel were injured and over 2,000 individuals with criminal antecedents reportedly participated in the protests, contributing to incidents of violence. As the situation escalated, clashes occurred, resulting in injuries to innocent students as well,â it added.

World.title: CJP protest: Airfares soar as train services hit; slight rise in last-minute bookings
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(With inputs from Chandigarh, Amritsar and Ludhiana)

NEW DELHI: The unprecedented clampdown in Delhi in the wake of CJP protest, including cancellation of several trains to the city, saw a "slight increase" in last-minute bookings on flights to and from Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA) for this weekend. Airfares on some routes saw a surge, too.Travel industry insiders said the shift could become more pronounced if the agitation and the restrictions on movement continue longer as the festive season begins Monday with Navratri."There has been a slight increase in bookings on Delhi flights for this weekend. It is too early to say anything for sure in terms of train and bus passengers moving to air as the weekend flights in the pre-festive season were pretty full and the fares were anyway high," said an airline official.A senior official of a leading online travel agency (OTA) said: "Till Friday night, we didn't see a major spike in spot fares from Lucknow, Prayagraj and other parts of UP. Only spot fares on Varanasi-Delhi route for Saturday were higher by 15% over a month back. So far, there is no substantial increase in flight demand."OTA sites showed Varanasi-Delhi one-way fares starting at Rs 6,200 and going up to Rs 14,000 Saturday - higher than usual.The big worry for airlines and Delhi airport is passengers, crew members and other staff being able to reach IGIA in time due to the feared large-scale disruption of metro service and impacted traffic movement.If the protest continues for a longer duration and pushes up demand for air travel, then airfares - which are anyway higher due to spiralling operating costs from higher jet fuel prices and a crashing rupee - will soar further, according to travel industry stakeholders.Airfares from Amritsar surged sharply Friday, with some flights touching Rs 8,000 against the usual one-way fare of around Rs 4,000. Fares for the Saturday flight from Ludhiana saw fluctuations throughout the day, soaring as high as Rs 12,987 before falling to Rs 4,301 at 8 pm."Those with onward travel plans, especially international flights, have limited choices and are having to buy expensive tickets to avoid further cancellations or missing their connections," said Dalip, a travel agent in Amritsar. There was no big change in flight and cab fares from Chandigarh to Delhi till Friday evening.

World.title: How many trains can one stop? Can't halt youth of India: Union minister Chirag Paswan
World.content: NEW DELHI: "They are the youth of India. Nobody can stop them," BJP ally and Union minister Chirag Paswan said Friday, replying to allegations that govt was curbing train and metro services to stop people from attending Saturday's protest called by CJP over the SIR issue."Some people are trying to spread such misconceptions. How many trains can one stop? How many roads can one block? They are India's youth, capable of showing the way to the world. Generations have done it. No one can stop them," the LJP (Ram Vilas) president told reporters on the sidelines of an event.After CEC Gyanesh Kumar came under scrutiny following the charge that he was taking unilateral decisions, Chirag had called for clarification but quickly backed out after Election Commission released a statement to suggest that decisions were unanimous.

World.title: I-T finds stamp duty, tax evasion in Karnataka land deals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tax authorities in Bengaluru have come across a new tool for evading taxes and stamp duty, a development that may have implications across states. Initial estimates suggest land deals of over Rs 300 crore have seen under-reporting.

The income tax department's directorate of intelligence and criminal investigation in the southern city has found several instances of incomplete disclosure of the entire sale consideration in the registered sale deeds.

The remaining amount is paid by executing unregistered full and final settlement deeds with the payment routed through banking channels.

There are several instances of the method being used by local builders to purchase land parcels and then develop them into residential units and plots.

"Since the additional payment made is not part of the sale deed, the buyer pays no stamp duty and registration fee to the state govt, resulting in huge revenue loss," said a person familiar with the probe.

The tax authorities have alerted the registration department in Karnataka. Stamp duty evasion in the state can result in hefty penalties.

Besides, the buyers did not deduct TDS despite purchasing 'urban agricultural land' as a result of which the additional amount paid through full and final settlement deed remained outside the radar of the tax department.





Some of the sellers, who have claimed exemption from the sale of agricultural land have not filed their returns, as a result of which tax was not paid.

"The department also identified a number of registered transactions involving exchange of property involving undervaluation of properties sold, on which there is short payment of stamp duty and registration fee and payment of additional consideration outside the book," said a person in the know.

"The circle rate is significantly lower than the market rate, which is resulting in these kind of transactions," an official said.

World.title: SC junks challenge to TN speaker's call to accept ADMK plea to condone 21 'rebels'

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Friday refused to entertain an AIADMK party worker's petition challenging the Tamil Nadu speaker's decision to accept AIADMK's plea to withdraw disqualification petitions against 21 of its legislators who had defied party orders and voted for the confidence motion moved by the governing TVK.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when the party, to which the MLAs belonged, has condoned the lapse and withdrawn its petitions seeking their disqualification, a person who is not even an MLA cannot challenge the speaker's decision.The petitioner said that by their very conduct, the 25 MLAs, of whom four have resigned, have indulged in anti-party activity and are liable for disqualification under the anti-defection law.The Supreme Court bench said in a multi-party democracy like India, political dynamics in a coalition govt must be left to the political parties and decisions in this regard by the speaker, unless palpably unconstitutional, cannot be interfered with by the courts.The Madras high court had earlier dismissed the appellant's writ petition against the speaker's order dropping disqualification proceedings against the 21 MLAs.

World.title: Judge recuses from Punjab government appeal case
World.content:
SC: Thousand sources... donât now where attacks will come

NEW DELHI: Justice Sheel Nagu, who was chief justice of Punjab and Haryana HC for nearly two years prior to his elevation to Supreme Court , on Friday recused from hearing Punjab govt's appeal against the HC's order directing a CBI probe into an alleged bribe syndicate, having links with the CM's OSD, that influenced postings, transfers and tenders.At the commencement of hearing, Justice Dipankar Datta said Justice Nagu wants to recuse from the case, even though senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Punjab govt, said the state did not have any objection to him remaining a part of the bench.Hinting that Justice Naguâs continuation on the bench might be turned into a controversy, Justice Datta said, âThese days there are a thousand sources. We do not know where the attacks will come.â In the recent past, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal had raised questions about a Delhi HC judgeâs impartiality and sought her recusal from hearing an appeal related to a criminal case against him.When Gupta reiterated his request, Justice Datta said SC has 17 benches and the case could go to another. The order stated: âRe-list this petition before a bench of which JusticeNagu is not a member.â

World.title: Assembly bypolls: TVK wins 2 seats in TN, BJP also bags 2 in Bengal
World.content:
A victory for political decorum and personal decency, says Vijay

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI/KOLKATA/PUDUCHERRY/GUWAHATI: TVK cleared its first test barely five months after forming govt in Tamil Nadu, winning the bypolls in two assembly constituencies, while in West Bengal, BJP retained Nandigram - CM Suvendu Adhikari's backyard - and wrested Rejinagar from AJUP (Aam Janata Unnayan Party), winning both assembly bypolls in its first electoral test since coming to office in state.All-India NR Congress, an NDA ally, retained Thattanchavady assembly segment, with Ashok Anand defeating his nearest Congress rival by over 8,400 votes. BJP regained Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency, with ex-IAS officer Devasish Sharma securing about 50% of the vote. AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal finished second, followed by Congress's Sibamoni Bora. Sharma, who was Nagaon district commissioner when he took VRS and had joined BJP last month, led Ajmal by over 1.5 lakh votes, while Bora trailed by over 1.2 lakh votes.Though Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu presented different political terrain, TVK won both seats with comfortable margins by fielding former AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama, who had joined the governing party barely 20 days after the assembly election results in May. Sathyabama won Dharapuram by 9,471 votes, while Maragatham secured Madurantakam with a margin of 20,040 votes.DMK finished second in both seats, while AIADMK, which had won the two segments in the April assembly election, was pushed to third. The results increase TVKâs strength in the 234-member assembly from 107 to 109. âThis is a victory for political decorum and personal decency. The victory is a verdict against derogatory remarks targeting women, personal attacks and betrayal. This winning streak will continue,â chief minister C Joseph Vijay posted on X.DMK president MK Stalin called it a âtemporary victory for betrayalâ.BJPâs two victories in Bengal take its strength to 209 in an assembly where it faces a fractured opposition, a part of which has been toeing the govt line on key issues. The saffron party retained Nandigram, where a bypoll was necessitated by Adhikariâs decision to vacate the seat in favour of Bhabanipur, by a record 1,22,753 votes.Adhikari had won Nandigram in the April assembly polls by 9,665 votes. Sanchita Dey Pradhan, fielded by Mamata Trinamool Congress, had withdrawn from the race on Sept 17 after meeting Adhikari in Kolkata. Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who finished second with the backing of Mamata Trinamool Congress, spent 11 days in police custody over FIRs lodged 19 years ago. He was able to campaign for only four days after Calcutta HC granted him interim bail on Sept 29.The comfortable wins in the Muslim-dominated seats of Nandigram and Rejinagar signal a potential shift in Bengalâs political arithmetic. In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won by 75,816 votes, pushing AJUP, which won the seat in the April poll, to second place. Muslims constitute 72% of the electorate in Rejinagar, in Murshidabad.

World.title: Vance's 'indentured servants' remark deeply offensive: Government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Following a long period of strained India-US ties, the gloves came off finally as India hit out at US Vice President JD Vance for labelling H-1B visa holders and foreign tech professionals as foreign indentured servants, a characterisation New Delhi slammed as deeply offensive and unwarranted.

The scathing response followed the US announcement about the suspension of many tech companies, including several from India, from PERM Green Card programme. Govt acknowledged the development may impact the permanent residency process of eligible employees even though the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of those visa holders and dependants will remain unaffected.

Vance had reinforced the announcement by declaring that American workers cannot be laid off and then replaced with foreign indentured servants.

He also insisted that only top-tier, elite foreign talent not available domestically should be brought into US.

MEA countered Vance's comments as it said in a statement that such descriptions were unwarranted.

MEA: Use of colonial legacy terminology deeply offensive

MEA said US Vice President JD Vanceâs comments also ignored the fact that Indian professionals in US are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem.

âIndeed, the history of the US itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity.





Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive,â said the ministry, adding it will continue to follow developments related to the issue.

The unusually blunt pushback suggests Indiaâs patience is wearing thin after a series of bilateral setbacks, ranging from trade and tariffs, immigration and talent mobility to Indiaâs ties with Russia and Washingtonâs Pakistan outreach.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar had recently warned that the USâ growing ties with Pakistan would hurt the India-US relationship.

The ministry also cautioned in its response that the steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries. It said talent mobility adds value to both economies, creating opportunities for Indians and helping US companies equally with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US.

âThis is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact,â said Indian govt.

While the America First signalling through the announcement seems designed for an electoral boost in the upcoming midterm polls, itâs unlikely to help the already rocky state of India-US ties. The timing is also problematic as it creates poor optics for PM Narendra Modiâs visit to the US in Dec for the G20 summit. It also comes just ahead of Secretary of State Marco Rubioâs visit to India this month, during which India will look to raise its concerns related to the issue.

World.title: Jaishankar highlights shared aspirations, self-reliance in India-Africa partnership
World.content:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Friday (October 9, 2026) highlighted the historic India-Africa partnership, rooted in shared solidarity and a common pursuit of fairness, representation, and the freedom to shape their own future, while outlining key areas of cooperation between the two sides.

Mr. Jaishankar arrived in Ethiopia on Thursday (October 8, 2026) from Côte d’Ivoire on the final leg of his three-nation tour of African countries, which also included Ghana.

Addressing a gathering at the Adwa Memorial Museum in Addis Ababa, Mr. Jaishankar said the development visions of India and Africa emphasised industrialisation, which should not be denied by flooding markets with cheap goods or restricting market access.

He highlighted the robust trade and investment ties between India and African countries across sectors such as manufacturing, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, energy, mining, agriculture, infrastructure, financial services and information technology.

Mr. Jaishankar said self-reliance was a shared conviction that provided a strong foundation for the enduring partnership between India and Africa.

India's development partnership with African countries was guided by the priorities of partner nations, he said, adding that India has "supported more than 220 projects" in areas such as "power generation, electricity transmission, water, agriculture, railways, healthcare, manufacturing and public infrastructure".

He also highlighted India's capacity-building initiatives, saying more than 70,000 African students and professionals had received support from India over the past decade.

Emphasising the growing role of technology in bilateral cooperation, Jaishankar pointed to the transformative impact of digital governance and expanding cooperation on India Stack.

"The transformative impact of digital governance, as well as growing India Stack cooperation with Africa. Space, drones, and AI are new frontiers of this cooperation," he said.

Mr. Jaishankar also underlined India's efforts to strengthen Africa's health security through vaccine support, pharmaceutical investments and the gifting of Bhabhatron cancer treatment machines.

In a separate post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said India and Ethiopia shared the vision of 'AI for All' and its potential to advance development and prosperity.

He also visited the Ethiopia Science Museum, describing it as a symbol of the country's efforts to build a technology-driven, knowledge-based economy. Science and innovation cooperation would play a greater role in the India-Ethiopia strategic partnership, he said.

World.title: Delhi Police detain at least 100 with criminal records in overnight ops. ahead of CJP protest
World.content:
Delhi Police have detained at least 100 people with criminal records in overnight operations across 15 districts, sources told The Hindu. They were allegedly suspected of joining Saturday’s (October 10, 2026) planned protest by the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) at Jantar Mantar amid the ongoing Election Commission row.

At least 100 people with criminal records have been detained across 15 districts of the national capital as part of a preventive measure, the source added.

Earlier, the Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing alleged non-compliance with conditions agreed upon during an earlier demonstration. Joint Commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Nupur Prasad said on Friday (October 9, 2026) that the permission was sought in the last minute while as per rules it should be sort atleast 10 days before the protest.

The CJP had maintained that it was informing the police rather than seeking permission, arguing that Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site and that the police should facilitate a peaceful gathering. Mr. Das had submitted the letter at Parliament Street police station and received an acknowledgement, according to the organisers.

As Delhi prepares for the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, traffic diversions will be enforced from 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 10, 2026), affecting movement at 30 key points across Delhi, police said.

Authorities have also taken several other measures ahead of the protest, including internet curbs in parts of Delhi, the shutting down of markets and Metro stations, and the cancelling dozens of trains bound for the capital.

With PTI inputs

World.title: Morning Digest: Delhi turns into a fortress ahead of CJP protest against CEC; INDIA bloc urges President to repeal recent Assembly polls, and more
World.content:
CJP protest: Trains cut, Internet down, Delhi turns into a fortress

The Delhi Police denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to hold its proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday (October 10), citing alleged violations of conditions agreed upon for an earlier demonstration, even as authorities rolled out an extensive security plan across the national capital. Despite the denial of permission, the CJP released a poster that says “Final Call To Save Democracy”, asking its supporters to reach Jantar Mantar at 10 a.m. on Saturday (October 10) as they look to go ahead with the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rollback of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

Repeal recent Assembly polls, INDIA bloc urges President

The Opposition INDIA bloc urged President Droupadi Murmu to “repeal” all Assembly elections held over the last two years, saying they have “incontrovertible proof” of “vote chori” (theft). Before their meeting with the President, the Opposition leaders gathered at the central hall of Samvidhan Sadan, where according to sources, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi claimed that the government is “rattled” and if the Opposition continues its campaign, the government could fall without completing its full term.

Ministry of Home Affairs directs States to prevent CJP supporters from mobilising towards Delhi

The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has asked all States and Union Territories to work with the Delhi Police and take preventive steps to stop protesters from mobilising towards the national capital. In a communication to Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police (DGPs), Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan flagged the “grave law and order and public order implications” of the proposed protest.

24-hour Internet shutdown ahead of Jantar Mantar protest, IT Ministry issues takedown advisory

As authorities gear up to tackle protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar, the capital is set to face stringent curbs on communication. The Delhi Police have imposed a 24-hour Internet shutdown around the protest site from 10 p.m. on Friday (October 9), while the Information Technology Ministry has urged social media platforms to quickly take down content referred to them by government Ministries and departments.

Delhi Police compile ‘database’ of potential protesters, make calls and visit homes ahead of October 10 Jantar Mantar protest

The Delhi Police have compiled a ‘database’ of people likely to participate in the October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar and are coordinating with law enforcement agencies across States to prevent them from reaching the capital, sources said. As part of the preventive measures, police in several States have detained potential participants, questioned supporters about their plans and visited their homes ahead of the proposed demonstration. The effort to intercept protesters at their starting points mirrors the Delhi Police’s district-wise strategy to prevent people from reaching central Delhi. With the protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organisations, the police are tracking potential participants through social media activity, intelligence inputs and coordination with State agencies, sources said.

Nothing can stop the youth of India: Chirag Paswan

Union Minister Chirag Paswan threw his weight behind the youth protest, while adding that there needs to be dialogue to resolve the current crisis. He also accused Opposition parties of politicising the issue. Responding to questions about the government clampdown ahead of Saturday’s protest, including the cancellation of trains headed to Delhi, internet shutdowns and the closure of Metro stations, Mr. Paswan said, “These are the youth of India. Nothing can stop them.”

Congress attacks Modi government over ‘promoting’ monopolies; says it will end crony capitalism

Targeting the Narendra Modi government for “promoting” monopolies, the Congress said India needs a level playing field where every business has a fair chance to compete. Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, said the Congress was committed to breaking the chain of crony capitalism. His remarks came a day after his exchange on X with U.S. billionaire Elon Musk, who asked whether Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani was the “real boss” of India.

Government slams Vance’s remarks on Indian IT professionals as ‘deeply offensive’

The Ministry of External Affairs slammed as “unwarranted” and “deeply offensive” U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance’s comments in which he called foreign workers, including Indian IT professionals, “indentured servants”. Hitting out at the U.S. government for its decision to suspend “labour certifications” from several Indian technology firms based in America, the Ministry said the steps would not “advance the shared ambitions of both countries”, indicating further trouble in the already difficult economic relationship between the two countries.

No surprises in byelection results in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry as voters favour the ruling party candidates

The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which came to power in Tamil Nadu exactly five months ago, passed its first electoral test in Tamil Nadu, bagging the Madurantakam and Dharapuram (Reserved) Assembly constituencies. In Puducherry, the ruling All India N.R. Congress (AINRC) retained Thattanchavady. Both in Madurantakam and Dharapuram, TVK nominees Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama were elected with comfortable margins of 20,040 votes and 9,471 votes respectively. They won from these constituencies in April-May 2026 as AIADMK candidates and then defected to the ruling party after resigning as MLAs.

BJP targets Rahul over exchange with Musk; counters SpaceX founder’s remarks on spectrum policy

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) criticised SpaceX founder Elon Musk for his remarks on India’s spectrum allocation policy, while taking a jibe at the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, over his exchange with Mr. Musk on X. “What is more surprising is that Mr. Rahul Gandhi, who earlier always used to accuse us of surrendering before the American leadership, is now championing the cause of Mr. Musk,” BJP national vice-president Ram Madhav told the media.

West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court mulls having tribunals first hear deleted voters seeking re-inclusion

The Supreme Court orally suggested that lakhs of voters seeking inclusion in the West Bengal electoral roll deserved to be heard first, while appeals for exclusion pending before the Appellate Tribunals could be heard last. An affidavit filed by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in the Supreme Court in September 2026 revealed that more than 22 lakh voters purged from the electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in West Bengal, on grounds such as “logical discrepancies,” had filed appeals challenging their exclusion.

BJP wrests Assam’s Nagaon Lok Sabha seat after seven years

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in central Assam after seven years, with its candidate Devasish Sharma bagging almost 50% of the votes polled on October 6. The underlying narrative of the BJP’s bypoll victory was its inroads into areas dominated by Muslims, mostly of Bengal origin, who became a majority in the constituency after the 2023 delimitation.

Eight BJP and two SP candidates from UP elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha

All 10 Rajya Sabha candidates from Uttar Pradesh -- eight from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and two from the Samajwadi Party (SP) -- were declared elected unopposed, an official said. “All the 10 candidates who were in the fray for the Rajya Sabha biennial elections -- eight from the BJP and two from the SP -- have been declared elected unopposed,” Returning Officer for the Rajya Sabha polls Ajit Verma told PTI.

Telangana to make strong pitch for resolution of bifurcation issues at MHA meeting on Oct 22

The State government has decided to focus on making a strong pitch for resolution of the pending bifurcation issues with neighbouring Andhra Pradesh. The government has entrusted the responsibility of presenting the State’s cause in the bifurcation issues to the Planning department. The subject matters of State Reorganisation of General Administration (SR-GC) Department, including the matters relating to Inter-State Council, Southern Zonal Council, and Punchi Commission, are allotted to Secretary to Government, Planning department - in addition to his regular duties.

West Bengal bypolls: BJP retains Nandigram with record margin, wins Muslim-dominated Rejinagar

The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won both Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly seats in West Bengal by a huge margin in the byelection that was held on October 6. In Nandigram Assembly seat located in Purba Medinipur district, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath won by a record margin of over 1.22 lakh votes. The margin of victory for BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar at Rejinagar in Murshidabad district was over 75,000 votes.

CTI seeks ban on protests in Delhi till Diwali, says business hit

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has demanded a ban on large-scale protests in Delhi’s key commercial and central areas from Navratri till Diwali, citing their impact on businesses. The outfit also urged the government to designate a permanent protest zone outside the city. In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal called for restrictions on large gatherings at Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street and Lutyens’ Delhi, saying repeated demonstrations and disruptions to metro services were affecting traders and customer movement.

Government rejects ‘omnibus’ claims of enrolment of NEET-UG protestors’ biometrics on criminal database

The union government has opposed Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim’s “sweeping” assertion that the biometric data of “thousands of protestors” has been enrolled on national criminal databases. An affidavit filed by the Home Ministry through the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) said blanket allegations of indefinite retention, storage and sharing of biometric information were not based on foundational facts.

Suspension of U.S. green card programme will not impact workforce strategy: TCS

Tata Consultancy Services Ltd (TCS) said that it would comply with any directive from the U.S. government to continue its business in the country, stating that the latest suspension of the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM) would not impact its workforce strategy or customer engagements. The statement comes after the U.S. suspended several IT firms, including Tata, from the PERM programme, which allows companies to apply for green cards for H-1B visa workers.

Assam student who called home about drunken men in train coach found dead near tracks in Andhra’s Srikakulam

A 21-year-old student from Guwahati who had called her family from a train to say she felt unsafe among drunken men in her coach was found dead beside the railway tracks in Andhra Pradesh’s Srikakulam district. The railway police suspect she fell from the running train; her family, however, alleges she was murdered.

Supreme Court asks for medical report of Kerala’s tallest captive elephant, pulls up State government

The Supreme Court pulled up the Keralam government for its failure to inform the court of the measures taken to protect Uttoly Raman, the State’s tallest captive elephant, after the tusker’s custody was handed over to the government in June. The court directed the authorities to place the latest medical examination report of the elephant, which has been at the centre of a long-running ownership dispute, before it on October 12.

Sri Lanka appeals to Saudi Arabia to overturn migrant worker’s death penalty

Sri Lanka is preparing to petition Saudi Arabia’s Supreme Court to overturn a recent Court of Appeal ruling sentencing a migrant worker to death. “We are working on an appeal and are hoping to file it today or tomorrow at the Supreme Court,” President’s Counsel Upul Kumarapperuma told The Hindu from Riyadh. He is part of a team of senior lawyers and officials from the public prosecutor’s office sent by the Sri Lankan government to Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Visual artist Angel-Rose Oedit Doebé turns pink rice into an archive of Indian and Surinamese identity
World.content:
There is something almost mischievous about Angel-Rose’s pink rice creations. It sits behind perspex, dyed pink, looking at first like confectionery or confetti or the aftermath of a children’s party. Then you notice the photograph, the television image, and then the rice again. By the time you have made the circuit, the object has acquired the uncomfortable density of an archive.

This is the trick the artist likes to play: make you look at something because it is pretty, and then make you stay because it is not.

The 31-year-old Amsterdam-based visual artist showcased her untitled series at Method in Delhi as part of Fresh Produce, the exhibition’s third edition, which brings together emerging artists from India alongside Angel-Rose. The series grew out of her research into the archives of OHM, the former Dutch broadcaster devoted to Indian, Surinamese and South Asian programming. Working with Beeld & Geluid, she found images from the 1990s and 2000s that returned to her something she had spent much of her childhood consuming at a distance: pop culture.

Rice, for Angel-Rose, carries several histories at once. It is food, plantation crop, material, memory. It also resembles the television static of the 1990s and early 2000s. “The works that I make currently are very minimal, but because of that, every decision is very precise,” she says.

The rice refers to the history of Surinamese-Hindustani people whose lives became entangled with Suriname's plantations. Angel-Rose’s family history is part of that story.

The artist grew up in the Netherlands with the visual vocabulary of Western pop culture: rhinestones, glossy surfaces, hyper-feminine clothes, excess, the delicious vulgarity of more is more. Later, she began recognising those same impulses in South Asian aesthetics: the jewellery, fabrics, saturated colour, elaborate wedding clothes, the refusal to apologise for taking up visual space. What had appeared to her as Western pop culture began to look, in part, like a culture whose origins had been badly edited.

“It was very difficult for me to really love my culture where I come from,” she says. Her mixed Indian, Surinamese and Caribbean background, she explains, was both a richness and a complication: Indian, Surinamese and Black ancestry, growing up in a predominantly white Western society, trying to understand which pieces belonged where.

Art became a way of putting those pieces back on the table. Her practice began in photography and expanded into installation, archival work and ready-made sculpture. The organising principle is what she calls the “angel-rose coloured glasses”, a phrase that borrows from the familiar instruction to look at the world more optimistically and turns it into a private universe. “If people want me to look through these rose coloured glasses, I will show you the world through my rose coloured glasses,” she says.

The glasses are pink, naturally. They are also rhinestone-studded, camp, funny and occasionally furious.

Her earlier works include I HOPE YOU HAVE THE CONFIDENCE OF A MEDIOCRE WHITE GUY TODAY, IF YOU ARE CIS, STRAIGHT AND WHITE THIS AIN’T FOR YOU, WHITEWASHED BUT STILL I LOVE YOU and Excluded from Reparations. There is a pleasure in those titles, but also a trap: they invite the viewer to laugh before making the laughter slightly difficult. In Bitch I’m a Cow, a sculpture of a cow becomes another such collision of references, its Dutch and Indian associations sitting beside one another.

Her flamboyance is deliberate. She is interested in what happens when things dismissed as “bimbo”, superficial or low culture enter the supposedly serious territory of contemporary art. Her pantheon includes Lady Gaga, Missy Elliott, Lil’ Kim, Dolly Parton, Rosalía and Charli XCX. Pop culture, she argues, is not a decorative side-room of society. It is one of the places where society reveals its appetites, prejudices and cruelties.

“Low culture can be highbrow. It can be high culture. It is very intellectual,” she says.

In her untitled series, rice becomes the hinge between ancestry and television, between plantation history and the pixelated snow of an old screen. Angel-Rose describes rice as a material of community, something people touch and eat together, but also as a material tied to the history of Surinamese-Hindustani labour. The rice is placed inside boxes, almost held hostage by the frame. The work is simultaneously image and object, memory and surface. Artsy describes the works as using print on perspex, rice, paint and archival material.

The pink is, inevitably, Angel-Rose. And then there are the cows, named Juliette, Jeanette and Bernadette after her great-grandmother and grandmothers. They came from India, along with the bricks, fabrics, traffic sounds and visual fragments she has gathered over several visits. Her phone contains a folder called “Brown History”, a private museum of things she sees and does not want to lose.

There is an earlier work called vroeger was je anders :$ wjnmk, a title that looks like the residue of an adolescent MSN conversation. The abbreviation means, roughly, “never want to lose you”, and the work circles memory, nostalgia, love and trauma. It is a useful key to Angel-Rose’s practice: she is suspicious of nostalgia when it is merely decorative, but deeply attached to what nostalgia can recover.

India has become part of that recovery. She has returned repeatedly, collecting images and conversations, meeting artists and women, watching the streets. She describes finding friends and peers here who make her feel, in her words, that she has “found my girls on the other side of the world”.

Yet she is careful about the position from which she looks. “I acknowledge that I grew up and I live in a Western country. So my perspectives are built on being from a Western country.”

Decolonisation, in Angel-Rose’s hands, is not a pose of arrival. It is a willingness to keep discovering that the thing you thought you knew had another beginning. The rice remains pink but the history inside it is considerably harder to colour.

World.title: Delhi braces for CJP protest: 45 metro stations shut, trains cancelled, 23,000 security personnel deployed
World.content:
As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), along with student organisations, social activists and farmer groups, gears up for a massive protest on Saturday (October 10, 2026), authorities have tightened security and imposed traffic restrictions across New Delhi.

The CJP, led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with other student bodies such as All India Students Association (AISA) and AISF, announced a nationwide march to Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the complete rollback of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Protestors allege that the SIR exercise is being misused to tamper with voter lists by deleting genuine voters, misclassifying living citizens as deceased despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive and altering key registration documents like Form 6 without consent.

45 metro stations closed

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has announced the closure of 45 metro stations on Saturday in view of the prevailing law and order situation. The move follows DMRC’s earlier order of closure of 57 metro stations, which got revoked after Supreme Court directed Central Government to lift stringent restrictions.

On Friday night, the DMRC posted in X, “Due to security reasons, the entry and exit at the following metro stations will remain closed from 09:00 PM on 9th October, 2026 till 06:00 PM on 10th October, 2026. Further the situation will be reviewed by the security agencies and necessary updates will be shared accordingly. However, interchange facility will remain available at all the concerned metro stations except New Delhi metro station”.

Major transit hubs such as Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Kashmere Gate, Hauz Khas, and Supreme Court are among the closed locations.

Trains cancelled and diverted

Similarly, railway zones across the country, including Western Railway, Central Railway, Northern Railway and North-Western Railway, have cancelled or rescheduled over 200 trains coming into or originating from Delhi citing severe road traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.

Western Railway rescheduled the Mumbai Central–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (12951) and August Kranti Rajdhani Express (12953) by five hours, while cancelling services like the Bandra Terminus–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (12247), Dr. Ambedkar Nagar–New Delhi Express (20155), Indore–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (09309), Indore–New Delhi Express (12415), and Sabarmati–New Delhi Express (12957). Central Railway cancelled the CSMT–Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express (22221) and CSMT–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (22209. The North Western Railway on Friday (October 9) cancelled 13 train services scheduled to depart for the national capital on October 9 and 10, citing “operational reasons”. Meanwhile, the Jammu railway division on Friday announced the cancellation of four key trains heading to the national capital, including the superfast Rajdhani Express.

This includes 75 Mail/Express including Rajdhani, Tejas, Shatabdi, and 170 passenger trains.

Railways has set up dedicated helpdesks and officials clarified that passengers with valid, verified train tickets will be allowed access to stations.

23,000 security personnel deployed

The Ministry of Home Affairs has provided the Delhi Police with additional companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) to strengthen security arrangements in view of the proposed protest and other potential gatherings in the national capital.

According to sources, around 23,000 security personnel are expected to be deployed across Delhi between October 8, 2026 and October 12, 2026.

The New Delhi area is expected to witness extensive security deployment on October 10, 2026, with multi-layered barricading, CCTV surveillance and Facial Recognition System (FRS)-enabled cameras being used to monitor movement.

Strict vigil will be maintained at Delhi’s borders, railway stations and bus terminals. Security agencies are also keeping a special watch to prevent criminal elements from entering protest gatherings by posing as protesters, sources said.

Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in force, and gatherings in violation of the restrictions will not be permitted.

Depending on the situation, police may also regulate access to metro stations and markets in the New Delhi area.

Security agencies are maintaining close coordination and monitoring developments ahead of October 10 to prevent any law-and-order situation in the national capital, sources said.

Other closures: schools, colleges, liquor shops shut

The Delhi government ordered all retail liquor vendors to remain closed on October 9, 2026 and October 10, 2026, citing the prevailing situation and the need to maintain public order. Multiple educational institutions including Sardar Patel Vidyalaya, shifted classes online and postponed scheduled events

Who are joining the CJP protest

Despite the Delhi Police denying permission for the protests, citing past rule violations and short application notice, several civil groups and prominent leaders have shown their interest in participating in the protests.

Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has announced that his family and he will join the protest at Jantar Mantar. AISA national president and student activist Neha Bora urged participants across the country to hold local sit-ins wherever they are. The demonstration will continue along with the Left student groups, farmers associations and civil rights groups.

CJP leaders including Mr. Dipke, Sayrav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will be leading the agitation.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: No meat, big money: Inside India’s lucrative boom in upscale vegetarian dining
World.content:
Thirty-four years ago, three graduates of the Institute of Hotel Management in Chennai came together to launch Eden Vegetarian in Besant Nagar. Known for its Continental fare — corn florentine, crepes, milagu sevai shashlik, mushroom on toast — the restaurant is still packed with diners every day.

Venkatesh Balakrishnan, director, Eden Vegetarian, says upscale vegetarian restaurants in Chennai were a rarity when he launched the outpost with Aparna Venkatesh and Subadhra Raju. “We had Sangeetha and Saravanaa Bhavan serving traditional South Indian fare, but not Continental cuisine. Pasta, for instance, was only on five-star hotel menus,” says Venkatesh, adding that they wanted their focus to be on Italian and Continental fare. “People still come for our dishes like corn on toast, and Madras risotto that is made with basmati rice.”

After they opened, Venkatesh says they were overwhelmed with the response, and Eden was packed through the week with diners coming from as far as Broadway. In 2004, the trio launched a second outpost at Harrisons Hotel, which did well until a pandemic-induced closure.

The standalone vegetarian restaurant rises

While India has always had a strong vegetarian customer base, offerings like Eden Vegetarian were trendsetters for their time. Over the decades, the industry has seen several new dining formats, chefs exploring varied cuisines, and a shift in the way Indians eat out. But, a trend that has quietly been making its way across our culinary landscape is that of the standalone vegetarian restaurant.

Latest outposts include The Kind Roastery and Brew Roomz, Continuum in Bengaluru; Paashh, Uppu in Mumbai; among others. A study by Data For India says that the share of Indian adults who eat meat rose to 80% in 2021 from 74% in 2006 (dataforindia.com). Yet, vegetarian menus are clearly on the rise everywhere.

Highlighting Indian plants and produce

Four years ago, Rajan Sethi, managing director, Bright Hospitality, launched OMO, a farm-to-table kitchen in Gurugram to spotlight “India’s diversity of produce, regional food traditions, and culinary techniques”.

He says going all-vegetarian was a conscious decision. “The idea was never to create a vegetarian restaurant by simply removing meat from the equation. It was about building the entire experience around what we could do with plants and Indian produce,” he states, adding that their menu changes with the season.

Over the last two years, Rajan — who also runs Ikk Punjab in the capital — has seen vegetarian dining “move beyond being defined by what it excludes to being defined by what it can offer”.

He says guests are becoming more curious about vegetables like lingdu (fiddlehead fern), regional Indian ingredients such as Gobindobhog rice, and the stories behind what they eat. “There is a growing appetite for more thoughtful, ingredient-led vegetarian experiences. A lot of our diners are not necessarily vegetarian, but they are increasingly open to choosing a meal based on the ingredient and the experience rather than whether it includes meat,” Rajan adds.

What diners demand

Most often that not, when people think of vegetarian food, they automatically gravitate towards South Indian food, but this is slowly changing, says Deval Shah, founder of Mumbai-based Tao 66, which offers a seven-course vegetarian Thai tasting menu. “As long as the food is good and authentic, people aren’t necessarily looking at whether it is South Indian, North Indian, Asian, or anything else. Fusion was definitely a big trend for a long time, but people are now coming back to authentic, classic dishes with interesting ingredients,” he says.

For owner-Chef Niharika Peri of Bengaluru’s Eatinn’ Love Trattoria, the decision not to serve meat at her establishment was due to several factors, and not just that she is a vegetarian. The restaurant — known for its Neapolitan sourdough pizzas, pastas, and ice creams — is popular among communities such as Jains and Marwaris, who are more comfortable with an all vegetarian kitchen, she explains.

A new wave

In Bengaluru the concept of vegetarian fine-dining has been around longer than most cities. “1947 Restaurant was one of the pioneers in scaling up the fine-dining vegetarian space across multiple branches,” says Prem Vatsav of Eat Theory Hospitality who recently launched Alé (wave, in Kannada). “The London Curry House was a major trailblazer in introducing the innovative vegetarian concept to the city,” he adds.

Prem, who also helms Bangalore Brew Works (currently under renovation), says that “180% of our revenue here comes from liquor”. “Earlier, I would never consider launching a restaurant without a bar license, but there has been a shift in the industry. During research for Alé, we found that a majority of diners are willing to pay top dollar for truly innovative vegetarian dishes. We also recognised the large Jain population in the Jayanagar market, which prompted us to intentionally focus on providing extensive Jain options,” says Prem.

He secured a bungalow built in the 1960s with his architect wife, Arpita Jain, designing the space. “We preserved the structure entirely without breaking an inch of the house, choosing instead to utilise its courtyard where the 100-seater Alé sits.” The alleyway has been put to use as an all-day coffee and matcha bar, Co,Ma, serving specialty coffees, matcha, and eggless bakes.

Addressing the rise in non-vegetarians opting for vegetarian meals, Prem talks about how “most modern Indian restaurants thrive due to their innovative menus, driven heavily by social media influencer marketing, which has sparked curiosity among non-vegetarian diners as well”. Prem admits that the clientele at Alé is different from Bangalore Brew Works, where the focus was more on the alcohol. “In a concept like Alé, diners need more attention. We also value their suggestions, take feedback, and the concept is more food-centric,” says Prem.

Bakeries that skip eggs

And it is not just QSR’s or fine-dining establishments cashing in on the market, but bakeries and cloud kitchens too. Like Neha S Nirmal and Nischal Vasant Meethal’s Fillo Bakes, a vegetarian Japanese-inspired moving bakery that launched in the Garden City in December 2025. “For years, a large part of the vegetarian audience skipped baked goods because most contain eggs. I have also noticed that customers ask more about ingredients: butter or margarine, jaggery or millets, instead of how processed it is in terms of refined sugar and maida,” says Neha, who offers shokupans, milk breads, savoury karepans, and anpans.

Considering Japanese variants have several meaty options, why did the duo veer away from these? “Being a fully vegetarian kitchen opens Fillo to a far larger audience: anyone can order for a family gathering, a festival or an office table,” says Neha who does not intend adding meat-based items. “Our category doesn’t need them. For us, butter does the work that eggs would normally do for texture, and we have tailored our range for India, where vegetables, millets and proteins offer enormous variety. Being clear about who we are matters more to me than a longer menu.”

For anything to work commercially, you really just have to know what you are putting into the business and what you are getting out of it, says Deval. “Whether you are a QSR, a fine-dining restaurant or a regional cuisine concept, there is space for all these formats to grow because, as a country, we’re looking for everything: a QSR when we’re on the move, a fine-dining restaurant for a special occasion, a regional restaurant when we’re craving something specific,” he says.

For Nischal, dealing with a buyer’s perception of Fillo Bakes as ‘vegetarian’ or ‘egg-free’ can be read as plain or limiting. “I have to prove it is neither”. “Another challenge is that of championing the craft: getting the right texture without egg means leaning on butter and technique, and keeping recipes stable without egg-based shortcuts takes time and skill,” he says, adding that sourcing and delivering temperature sensitive products in a climate like India is a logistics challenge of its own.

A menu that evolves

For Rajan, one of the biggest challenges is that he cannot rely on familiar formats or a protein-led centre of the plate to create excitement. “You have to constantly think about how to give vegetables and Indian ingredients enough depth, texture and character to make the experience feel complete. That pushes us to keep experimenting with seasonality, fermentation, preservation, live-fire cooking, and lesser-known Indian ingredients. It also means the menu has to keep evolving with what is available, rather than becoming repetitive,” he says, adding that the per-table spend on a weekday is approximately ₹6,000, which goes up to ₹10,000 on weekends.

At Alé, Prem says his share of operational and market challenges includes service staff requiring extensive training and constant supervision to ensure strict SOPs are followed during all guest interactions. “Manpower requirements are higher when compared to running a same-sized pub in the city, as a lot of elements must seamlessly align to execute the experience properly. There is also a continuous need to change and adapt the menu based on guest feedback,” he says, adding that a new menu is set to launch later this month. At Alé, he serves about 100 guests on a weekday and approximately 300 covers (per day) on a weekend, with an average spend of ₹800 per guest.

Banking on business

“During my initial research, industry experts told me a vegetarian restaurant will never shut; it will always be profitable,” says Niharika. “During my early days, I have faced walkouts when diners realised there was no meat on the menu. But today, regardless of their dietary preferences, diners are now happy with an all vegetarian menu, especially when it is not a multi-cuisine restaurant.”

Nischal says people pay for vegetarian food when the quality is evident, not because of the label. “For us, being fully vegetarian widens the audience instead of narrowing it, and a vegetarian kitchen is operationally simpler too. Good butter and dairy, quality ingredients and labour-intensive techniques are not cheap, so I cost every recipe carefully and bake to order rather than guess at demand,” he explains.

OMO, Rajan says, “was built with the belief that a vegetarian restaurant can command the same value as any other fine-dining experience, provided the food, ingredients and overall experience justify it”.

World.title: Kerala HC order against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan and others raises a larger question of natural justice, say legal experts
World.content:
The Kerala High Court order asking the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to register an FIR against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, and his son-in-law and MLA P.A. Mohamed Riyas, has raised larger questions of natural justice and court orders overlooking the statutory provisions of law, according to legal experts.

Though the single judge elaborately heard the petitioner K.M. Shajahan and the Enforcement Directorate, which forwarded a letter to the State government seeking to register an FIR against the trio, the three were not offered an opportunity to be heard. The denial of the opportunity to be heard could be construed as the denial of natural justice. It will legally enable Mr. Vijayan and the two others to challenge the single judge’s order before the High Court or Supreme Court, judicial sources pointed out.

The order of the single judge, according to some legal experts, bypassed Section 17 (A) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which mandated prior approval from the competent authority for police officers to conduct inquiry into offences committed by public servants in the discharge of their official functions.

As a safeguard

The Section was introduced through an amendment in 2018 as a safeguard for government servants against unnecessary litigation, which could deter them from discharging their duties in an honest and fair manner. The question whether a court can overlook the statutory provisions of law that mandate prior approval for booking the case is pending before the Supreme Court. The matter was left for the consideration of a larger Bench of the court as the judges who heard the challenge came out with opposing judgments. Hence, the legality of the single judge’s action in ordering the registration of the FIR too could be challenged before the appropriate forum, sources indicated.

The State government, represented by Advocate General K. Jaju Babu, had contended that the competent authority should have an option to register an FIR or conduct a preliminary inquiry on receiving information from the ED. The State, which is left with limited legal options following the order, is unlikely to go on appeal.

The State could have played a crucial role in deciding the fate of the case had its prior sanction been sought under Section 17 (A) of the Act to prosecute the three. The legal responsibility of challenging the decision is left with Mr. Vijayan and the two others, legal sources indicated.

Does not apply to Veena

Meanwhile, the Vigilance will have to book an FIR against Mr. Vijayan and Mr. Riyas under the provisions of the Act. The ED would make use of the FIR and the allegations of corruption as a predicate offence to book Mr. Vijayan and Ms. Riyas for money laundering under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The Act will not apply to Ms. Veena who is not a public servant. However, the ED had proceeded against her based on the criminal complaint filed by the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) in relation to the alleged corporate fraud committed in Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) and Exalogic Solutions Pvt. Ltd., the firm owned by her.

Incidentally, the fate of the case against Ms. Veena would depend upon the outcome of the petition filed by CMRL before the Delhi High Court challenging the SFIO investigation.

World.title: Nepra clears use-of-system charges for competitive power market
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Nat­ional Electric Power Reg­ulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday notified use-of-system charges (UoSC) ranging from Rs6.23 to Rs19.62 per unit for bulk power consumers (BPCs) of all distribution companies, including K-Electric, participating in the competitive electricity trading market.

Under the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM), open-access consumers participating in the upcoming 400MW auction will have to pay Rs6.23 to Rs19.62 per unit to use the national grid for transporting electricity from the supplier to the consumer.

The UoSC includes transmission and distribution charges, a fixed grid charge and cross-subsidy.

A B-3 industrial consu­mer will be charged Rs6.23 per unit, while a B-4 industrial consumer will pay Rs9.09 per unit. These charges will be in addition to the electricity supply price, including generation cost, to be agr­eed between the private-sector supplier and the BPC.

At present, there are a little over 3,000 BPCs across the country.

The UoSC for C-3 and C-2 single-point distribution consumers has been notified at Rs14.95 to Rs19.62 per unit, while A-2 and A-3 general supply consumers will be charged Rs19.14 per unit. Agricultural consumers will pay Rs6.72 per unit.

For BPCs not participating in the competitive wheeling auction, UoSC rates have been set significantly higher, ranging from Rs19.17 to Rs32.56 per unit, depending on the consumer category.

In this category, B-3 and B-4 consumers will pay Rs19.17 and Rs25.45 per unit, respectively, while C-2 and C-3 consumers will be charged Rs31.30 and Rs32.56 per unit. A-2 and A-3 consumers will pay Rs32.08 per unit, while agricultural consumers will be charged Rs19.66 per unit.

A fixed grid charge of Rs1 per kilowatt per month, based on sanctioned load, will also apply to both categories, irrespective of whether they participate in the competitive auction.

The commercial market operation date for the CTBCM had already been declared as Jan 22, 2026, with the first market auction originally scheduled for June. However, the auction was delayed because UoSC charges had not been determined and notified.

The notification of uniform UoSC rates for all distribution companies and K-Electric is intended to pave the way for the formal launch of the competitive wholesale electricity market.

The Independent System Operation (Ismo), a new power division entity, is expected to auction 400MW of electricity in the first phase within the next couple of months. The government has allocated a total of 800MW for auction in two phases.

Nepra had forwarded its UoSC determination to the government for uniform application after considering the views of the power division, Ismo, K-Electric and BPCs on the mechanism for calculating and settling the charges, including inter-Disco differentials, cross-subsidies and transmission and distribution losses.

Under government directives, the impact of inter-Disco differentials arising from uniform UoSC rates will not be borne exclusively by wheeling consumers.

Nepra had also circulated a draft adjustment mechanism for settling inter-Disco differentials among relevant stakeholders.

The regulator said the key principle was to ensure that UoSC applicable to open-access consumers remained equal to those applicable to similarly pla­ced consumers of suppliers of last resort (SOLRs).

Based on the transmission and distribution losses of individual Discos, Nepra determined a uniform loss factor of 8.04pc at the 11kV level. For consumers connected at 132kV, it approved a uniform loss factor of 1.51pc, as proposed by the power division.

Nepra ruled that any additional charge required to cover differentials among Discos or K-Electric would apply to all consumers, including open-access consumers and those of SOLRs, thereby maintaining uniformity.

The federal government had earlier approved framework guidelines for the competitive wheeling auction of 800MW of electricity and for moving towards integrated energy planning across the country.

Under the framework, 800MW of generation capacity will be sold through competitive auctions for five years. The quantum could gradually increase after the initial trial, subject to government approval.

Ismo will now hold the first 400MW auction under a process approved by Nepra a few days ago. It is also expected to announce the auction calendar and detailed procedure shortly.

There will be no upper or lower limit on bid values, which will remain fixed for one year.

According to timelines set under the IMF programme, approval of the auction guidelines had been targeted for December, while approval of uniform wheeling charges by Nepra was due in January 2026.

Published in Dawn, October 10th, 2026

World.title: Afridi invites people from across country to join PTI's long march at Swabi Interchange on Oct 11
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi invited people from across Pakistan to reach the Swabi Interchange on Oct 11, where the PTI plans to announce the next steps for its long march that is being carried out to demand the release of jailed party founder Imran Khan.

The route plan for the march has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4. While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 11, beyond Swabi.

So far, the march has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

CM Afridi briefly also addressed participants on the way to Charsadda and told them not to worry as “we have to go elsewhere as well after Swabi”.

Afridi termed the federal government’s warnings “empty threats” and told the march participants that it “cannot harm the workers after they will cross the province’s boundary”.

The PTI march began after weekend talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. The federal ministers have warned the PTI not to lead the march beyond KP, and are also linking differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

In his address after reaching Charsadda, CM Afridi said convoys from Peshawar and Malakand divisions would reach the Swabi Interchange on Oct 13, while a course of action for Hazara Division would also be announced on the same day.

Convoys from Kohat Division would also reach the Swabi Interchange, while convoys from Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan Divisions would join the march along the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor route, he said, according to a statement issued by his office.

The CM urged the people to play their role in the “struggle for Haqiqi Azadi and sovereignty”.

He said he wished to place before the public a record of the past years, detailing the performance of the federal government following Imran’s ouster as the prime minister in 2022.

“Following the regime change operation, Pakistan’s economic indicators have been showing a negative trend. Pakistan has risen to the top of the Global Terrorism Index, and the country is now bearing the consequences of decisions taken behind closed doors,” he remarked.

According to Afridi, 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations have been conducted in KP between 2004 and 2026.

“Yet, terrorism has not been eliminated,” he said.

He said the people of KP, along with police and military personnel, were “making daily sacrifices and embracing martyrdom”.

CM Afridi added, “Whenever I spoke about formulating a policy to eliminate terrorism, my recommendations are not given due consideration.”

The CM also decried the alleged non-provision of funds from the Centre to KP.

Kundi’s challenge

Earlier in the day, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi challenged PTI protesters to dare and cross Swabi, a KP district that borders Punjab’s Attock and which the opposition party in the Centre has announced as the eventual destination of its long march..

Kundi raised doubt on the realisation of the PTI’s plan to reach Swabi on Oct 11.

“They are probably going to Charsadda today, then they might go to Mardan, and after that they might end up reaching Afghanistan through Dir,” he said while addressing a press conference in Peshawar. “Because whenever they turn towards Swabi, their legs start shaking, and their hearts tremble […] If they have any self-respect, reach Swabi tomorrow and cross it, or even step inside it. I will accept that you are a revolutionary party that aims to make a naya (new) Pakistan.”

Continuing to rail against the party, he said senior PTI leaders were “sitting in drawing rooms” in Islamabad while others were in “hiding”.

“They say that they have run successful mobilisation campaigns across Sindh and Punjab; did you see anyone from these provinces on their long march’s truck?” he questioned.

Reacting to the PTI’s claims that KP lawmakers and cabinet members were being “abducted”, Kundi said: “You (KP CM Afridi) should tell who is abducting your ministers as you are the chief executive of the province.

“You cannot protect your ministers, MPAs, and MNAs; how will you protect my people, the province and the nation? This is your position.”

Kundi added that the KP CM and his cabinet should resign on “ethical grounds”.

“They say that the SHOs do not listen to them; if no one listens to you, then why are you sitting [in the government]? Only to make money or for corruption,” he remarked, adding that presently, doctors, teachers, nurses, and municipal officers were observing strikes in KP.

The KP governor vowed that “we will protect our province and fight against terrorism on the front line. We will show such incompetent people […] how a province is run.”

Answering a question, Kundi contended that no province could run without the Centre. “But these people talk about confrontation with the federal government,” he said.

On the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the governor said that when the president or the prime minister deems that the situation in the province has worsened to the extent that these options should be availed, they would make a decision.

“Whenever the federal government will seek report on province’s situation; we will provide as per the information we have,” he added.

In response to another question, Kundi took a jibe at the PTI, saying the party had turned its long march into “Lucky Irani Circus, travelling from city to city […] But whenever they turn to Swabi, they opt to take a U-turn”.

He also commented on his recent meeting with KP’s chief secretary and inspector general (IG) to discuss the province’s law and order situation.

The KP CM has taken strong exception to the meeting and called for legislation to provide for the governor’s impeachment for “violating the Constitution”.

Kundi defended the meeting, saying: “I called the chief secretary and IG because we have no government on the ground in the province; they are busy in their circus.”

“My province is burning,” he continued, citing recent incidents of terrorism in KP.

“They (PTI) have never condemned terrorism. They cannot challenge the terrorists […] They don’t have any plan to fight terrorism,” he claimed.
